events.text: In the Wall-Ring of the old heavens stands a seal-door nobody opens, and today it knocks. Three taps, a pause, three taps. The wardens say it does this once a century and always stops. This time it has not stopped for nine days.

choices.text: Press an ear to the seal

effects.log: The stone is cold and humming, and the knocking comes up through your jaw like a second pulse.

choices.text: Ask the wardens for the seal-book

effects.log: The wardens bring it out reluctantly, a ledger bound in grey kelp, and open it for you.

choices.text: Leave it to the wardens

effects.log: You walk on. Behind you the knocking goes on, patient as a tide.

events.text: Through the seal comes a voice, very faint, counting. It is counting prayers: one, one, one, a god who has kept the tally of a sealed pantheon for longer than the domains have had names.

choices.text: Count along with the voice

effects.log: You count aloud, matching the cadence. The voice falters, then hurries, as if relieved to be heard.

choices.text: Say your name through the seal

effects.log: The counting stops dead. After a long silence the voice says your name back, mispronounced the way the old gods did.

events.text: The seal-book says the door was shut from outside by three gods, and only two signatures are there. The third line holds a thumbprint in ash, and the ash is still warm.

choices.text: Press your thumb to the warm ash

effects.log: The ash takes your print and the knocking changes: two taps, and a pause that sounds like a question.

choices.text: Copy the ledger and show it at court

effects.log: The court is very interested and very slow. By the time they act, you have learned the door is in no hurry either.

events.text: The tally ends at a number the old pantheon chose to stop at. The voice says thank you, and the seal-door goes quiet for the first time in nine days. On the stone a small sign appears, lines of faith like frost: what was owed to them, paid.

choices.text: Take the frost-lines as faith

effects.log: The frost melts into your hands, warm and strange: the last tithe of a pantheon that had no one left to pay.

choices.text: Leave the frost for the wardens to keep

effects.log: You leave it. The wardens bow. The seal-door stays quiet, and so, you think, does something very old.

events.text: The seal opens a hand-width and a smell comes out, old rain on a hearthstone. A voice says: tell the new gods we kept our word. Then the gap closes, and does not knock again.

choices.text: Carry the message to the high court

effects.log: The court is startled to learn the old pantheon still thinks it has a say. You are, for a season, the god who spoke to the wall.

choices.text: Keep the message, and tell no one

effects.log: Some words are safer in one head. You visit the door once a year and never knock.

events.text: At the seal of a walled-off heaven you find {npc}, a warden, sitting on a camp-stool as if the post were a fishing spot. {He} was told to guard it until relieved. That was before the war of the gods had a name.

choices.text: Offer to relieve {him} for a day

effects.log: You take the stool. {npc} stretches, stands, and walks away from the post in a daze, like someone out of the sea.

choices.text: Share a meal and the news

effects.log: You tell {him} what became of the war. {npc} listens to all of it, and says the thing nobody wanted to hear: so it ended.

choices.text: Admire the post and move on

effects.log: You nod to a duty older than your domain. {npc} nods back without turning.

events.text: While you hold the post, the seal breathes on your face, warm as a kiln. Something behind it is not dead; it is waiting, and you are the first new thing to stand at the door in an age.

choices.text: Read the seal as it breathes

ok.log: You read it: a sleeping heaven, nothing worse. It dreams of its own gardens.

fail.log: The seal stays a blur of warmth. You hold the post and learn nothing but patience.

choices.text: Hold still and say nothing

effects.log: You do what the warden did. By evening you understand why {he} stayed: the waiting has a kind of music.

events.text: {npc} asks you something small: whether the sea still smells of salt. {He} has not been able to remember, and it has begun to trouble {him} more than the seal.

choices.text: Bring {him} a shell of seawater

effects.log: You fetch a bowl from the Sea domain. {npc} breathes it in with closed eyes and weeps without noise.

choices.text: Bring {him} the sea itself: a day by the shore

effects.log: The shore, the gulls, a long grey light. {npc} sits on the sand all afternoon and does not say a word.

events.text: {npc} comes back to the seal at dusk and takes the stool. The post is {his} home and the wait is a kind of faith. {He} thanks you and asks you only to remember that someone stayed.

choices.text: Promise to remember, and carve the name

effects.log: You carve {his} name in the seal-rim, small and plain. The seal warms slightly beneath the cut.

choices.text: Promise to send a relief guard

effects.log: You send two young gods. {npc} is unimpressed but the post is never empty after.

events.text: The warden is still at the seal when you are old, and the stool has worn two grooves in the floor. {He} no longer speaks of the war. When you ask whether {he} is happy, {he} says that the seal is, and that is enough.

choices.text: Bring a second stool

effects.log: Two gods on two stools, guarding a quiet door. It is not a post any more, it is a friendship.

choices.text: Leave the warden in peace

effects.log: Some posts are best left to the one who holds them. You nod, and go.

events.text: A burned shrine in a low valley, roof gone, altar black. A scrap of banner still reads: for the god of the third hour. Nobody in your domain remembers there was a third hour god. Nobody remembers who burned it.
events.arc: The Shrine of the Third Hour

choices.text: Sweep the altar clean

effects.log: You sweep until the stone shows grey and then a pale rose under the soot. The wind lifts your hair as if approving.

choices.text: Search the ashes for what was kept

effects.log: In the ashes: a bronze bell with no clapper, and a child's tooth wrapped in silk.

choices.text: Say a short prayer to whoever was here

effects.log: The prayer drifts up and away. For a moment the valley seems to listen.

events.text: At the third hour the next day, the bell rings with no clapper. A thin figure stands in the roofless nave and looks at you with enormous patience. It is the god of the third hour, nearly worn out of existence.
events.arc: The Shrine of the Third Hour

choices.text: Offer the god a place in your shrine

effects.log: The thin god nods. You lend a corner of your faith, and a faint hour of the afternoon becomes theirs again.

choices.text: Ask who burned the shrine

effects.log: The thin god lifts a hand, points at the sky, and says a single name. It is not a name you want to hear.

events.text: The bell and the tooth together make a small sound that is almost a lullaby. You realise the shrine was a child's: a god of one hour, held in the arms of one worshipper who loved the evening.
events.arc: The Shrine of the Third Hour

choices.text: Return the tooth to the burned altar

effects.log: You set it on the stone. A single rose-coloured light ticks on, once, and goes out.

choices.text: Take the bell to your own shrine

effects.log: You hang it by your door. At the third hour each day it rings, and your shrine-keeper wonders why.

events.text: The god of the third hour grows a little less thin each year. At last you are shown the true size of the debt: a god lost an hour of the day, and nobody noticed for ten thousand years. They ask only that you keep the hour.
events.arc: The Shrine of the Third Hour

choices.text: Keep the third hour sacred in your domain

effects.log: Every day at the third hour your domain falls quiet. The thin god brightens with a sound like laughter in another room.

choices.text: Teach three other gods to keep it

effects.log: Four shrines now keep the hour. The third-hour god no longer fears being forgotten, only being sung too much.

events.text: The name the thin god spoke was a god of the high court, and you can say nothing without proof. But the ashes held a clue: a ribbon of ceremony-cloth stamped with the court seal.
events.arc: The Shrine of the Third Hour

choices.text: Confront the god quietly, in private

effects.log: The god pales, then speaks of an old fear: a god of an hour had grown too loved. The matter is settled with an apology and a quiet shrine.

choices.text: Keep the ribbon and wait

effects.log: You hide the ribbon. A grudge held lightly is a long thing; you will know when to use it.

events.text: In the cold ruin of a shrine, a hound lies on the altar-step, grey as the ash around it. It has been guarding something nobody remembers for as long as nobody remembers. It lifts its head when you come, and does not growl.
events.arc: The Hound of the Burned Shrine

choices.text: Sit down beside it

effects.log: The hound lays its head on your boot. Its fur smells of old smoke and rain.

choices.text: Offer it food from your shrine

effects.log: It eats slowly, thanking you with its eyes. Then it rises and walks to the altar and waits.

choices.text: Back away and leave it to its guard

effects.log: The hound watches you go, without reproach.

events.text: The hound leads you under the altar to a stair that no fire reached. Down below, a god's cold hearth, and in it an ember still alive, small as a seed.
events.arc: The Hound of the Burned Shrine

choices.text: Carry the ember out in your hands

effects.log: It does not burn you. It pulses once like a heartbeat and rests in your palm.

choices.text: Leave the ember and ask the hound its name

effects.log: The hound has no name for itself, only for the god it served. It whispers a word that smells of bread.

events.text: The hound stands guard while you eat at the altar-step, and it begins to speak in the voice of the god who owned it: gruff, kind, quick to laugh. It is not the hound talking, it is the memory the hound holds.
events.arc: The Hound of the Burned Shrine

choices.text: Listen all night

effects.log: By dawn you know a forgotten god's recipes, jokes and a dozen small tenderness. You hold them like a book.

choices.text: Ask the memory a question

effects.log: It answers with a story, which was the god's way of answering everything.

events.text: The ember in your hands has begun to grow. The hound follows you home and takes the doorstep of your shrine as if it had always done so. Your shrine-keeper stares: the hearth, for the first time in a century, will not go out.
events.arc: The Hound of the Burned Shrine

choices.text: Light a lamp from the ember in the old god's name

effects.log: The lamp burns a clear amber. The hound sleeps beside it, unafraid for the first time in an age.

choices.text: Return the ember to its stair

effects.log: You put it back and sit with the hound. It will keep guarding, but it is no longer alone: you visit each spring.

events.text: The hound has the name for the god now: you speak it aloud in the burned nave, and the wind lifts it. Somewhere very far away a shrine bell rings. The hound lies down, finally, for the first long sleep it has had in an age.
events.arc: The Hound of the Burned Shrine

choices.text: Sit with it until it wakes

effects.log: It sleeps three days. You do not leave. When it wakes it is only a dog.

choices.text: Carve the name above the altar

effects.log: The name stays in the stone, unburned. People begin to leave offerings there, not knowing why.

events.text: Beyond a plain stone bridge hangs a sealed heaven locked nine times, and eight locks are already open. The ninth is warm. Someone has been here before you, and left in a hurry.

choices.text: Search the open locks for tracks

effects.log: Eight keys lie on the bridge, all left behind. The tracks lead away, but not far.

choices.text: Open the ninth lock yourself

effects.log: The lock turns without a click. Behind the gate there is a smell of cut hay and a distant bell.

choices.text: Leave the bridge untouched

effects.log: You let the ninth lock stay. Some doors are better closed even if their keepers have fled.

events.text: Inside the sealed heaven is a meadow under a low copper sky and a herd of pale beasts grazing, unharmed by an age of waiting. At the far end, a gate-keeper god is asleep with a ring of keys on the belt.

choices.text: Slip the keys off the sleeping keeper

ok.log: The keys come free without a jingle. You have the keeper's whole trust in your hand.

fail.log: A key rings. The keeper wakes, smiling blankly, and bids you welcome in a voice of cold steel.

choices.text: Wake the keeper gently

effects.log: The keeper wakes with a start, then lies back with relief: I thought you were the one coming to take the herd.

events.text: The tracks end at a boat-landing. A traveller has gone to sea and not returned, but a pack was left behind: a sealed letter, a half-finished map of the nine locks, a dried flower pressed in a prayer.

choices.text: Read the letter

effects.log: It is a confession: the traveller opened eight locks and lost nerve at the ninth. They begged whoever came next to finish it.

choices.text: Carry the pack back to the court

effects.log: The court thanks you and does nothing, as is its way.

events.text: The herd lifts its heads together. The keeper says the beasts have waited for the lock to open since the day the gods walled them off to save them from a war. They ask only for a field outside the walls.

choices.text: Lead the herd out to the Green Assembly's meadows

effects.log: The herd streams out like pale rain. The keeper weeps and finally sleeps for real.

choices.text: Keep the heaven sealed, and visit

effects.log: You close the ninth lock again. The herd will wait a little longer, but now they know a god who visits.

events.text: The keeper's keys are warm in your hand. With them you could shut the heaven forever, or open it to the whole realm. The herd is calm. The choice, for once, is yours alone.

choices.text: Open all gates and release the herd

effects.log: The meadow rolls out into the realm. The beasts scatter, grateful and bewildered, into the domains of Life and Beasts.

choices.text: Keep the keys, and tell no one

effects.log: You carry the keys quietly. The sealed heaven has a new guardian and the herd a patient friend.

events.text: Among the black beams of a burned temple, {npc} is writing prayers in charcoal on the walls. {He} says each one is for a god who has none, and {he} has been at it since before your domain was cut.

choices.text: Ask {him} to write one for you

effects.log: The charcoal is dry and sweet. {npc} writes a short line, a small blessing, and steps back to see whether you like it.

choices.text: Help {him} write the rest

effects.log: Side by side you scrawl names of gods nobody sings. The wall begins to look like a small, patient chorus.

choices.text: Admire the work and go

effects.log: The walls are crooked with devotion. You take a long look before you leave.

events.text: The charcoal prayers begin to glow at dusk, line by line, as if the gods named in them had heard. {npc} is not surprised. {He} says it happens once in a lifetime, and this is {his} third.

choices.text: Ask what the gods answered

effects.log: {npc} shows you a wall where the charcoal has darkened into a different hand: answers, written back, in a script from before the domains.

choices.text: Add a prayer of your own

effects.log: Your line glows with the rest. Somewhere, a god who has lost the habit of being asked looks up.

events.text: The blessing {npc} wrote for you has stayed warm on your shrine wall. Visitors notice it and ask about the strange hand. You find you are proud of it.

choices.text: Invite {npc} to write all your shrine walls

effects.log: The priest accepts with a grave bow. Your shrine becomes a house of crooked, tender lines.

choices.text: Keep the blessing as a private thing

effects.log: You guard it quietly. It is enough to know it is there.

events.text: {npc} is very old when {he} writes the last line, a prayer for the god who burned the temple. {He} does not know who it was. {He} says forgiveness is the only prayer that never needs the answer.

choices.text: Add your name to the prayer

effects.log: You write beside {him}. The charcoal burns bright for a breath and fades, as if relieved.

choices.text: Carry the prayer to the high court

effects.log: The court reads it in silence. Three gods quietly add their names, and nobody says why.

events.text: The priest dies at the wall one winter, charcoal in hand, a prayer half-written. You finish the line. Your hand shakes, but the words come: thank you for the light. The wall glows. In your shrine, the bell rings alone.

choices.text: Bury {him} in the nave

effects.log: The ash takes {him} like water. A small hearth-flame stays by the grave, burning with no fuel.

choices.text: Keep writing in {npc}'s place

effects.log: You pick up the charcoal. Someone has to.

events.text: A sealed heaven is scratched on the inside with tally marks, row after row, in six hands. At the end of the rows is a drawing of a door, and beside the door a stick-figure with a crown pointing out. Beneath it, in a smaller hand: still here.

choices.text: Scratch a mark of your own beside theirs

effects.log: You scratch a small mark. Somewhere beyond the wall, something answers with a faint scrape.

choices.text: Report the heaven to the wardens

effects.log: The wardens add it to a very long list and thank you for the courtesy.

events.text: The sealed-heaven wardens keep a tea-house at the foot of the wall, because the wait is long and the tea is the only thing that has ever changed. They serve you in the chipped cup nobody else is allowed to use.

choices.text: Drink slowly and hear their stories

effects.log: You hear a century of small events: a seal that sneezed, a moth that crossed three walls, a warden who took up poetry.

choices.text: Leave a small offering for the wall

effects.log: The wardens bow. Next year, they say, the tea will taste of whatever you left.

events.text: A sealed heaven drifts at the edge of the world in a fog so thick it feels like cloth. You can hear a flute inside, the same eight notes over and over, the beginning of a song nobody finished.

choices.text: Hum the ninth note

effects.log: The fog parts for a heartbeat. The flute stops, then plays the ninth note back, and a second voice joins it.

choices.text: Leave the song to its sleepers

effects.log: You turn away and let the eight notes continue. Some songs are not yours to finish.

events.text: You find a seal so old it has begun to rust, red lace crawling over what had been bright gold. A warden pats it fondly and says it needs a new coat of faith every thousand years. Yours would do.

choices.text: Give the seal a coat of your faith

effects.log: The rust shrinks back like a tide. The seal gleams and the warden pats your arm.

choices.text: Ask what is behind the rust

effects.log: The warden shrugs. Nobody remembers. That, they say, is what a good seal is for.

events.text: A sealed heaven the size of a bread-oven, wedged in the corner of a pantheon's attic, with a note: do not open, it is only a very small war. You can hear tiny trumpets.

choices.text: Leave it sealed and apologise to the trumpets

effects.log: The trumpets stop, then start again, more cheerfully.

choices.text: Slide a note under the lid: please stop

effects.log: The trumpets pause, as if reading. After a long moment, a tiny flag is held up, and fought over.

events.text: On the black step of a burned shrine someone has left a tithe of three coins of faith, warm and fresh, still glowing. Nobody has worshipped here in an age. Someone is paying anyway.

choices.text: Wait to see who comes

effects.log: At dusk a small child comes, leaves another tithe, and does not look up. The child vanishes between two blinks.

choices.text: Take a coin as a keepsake

effects.log: The coin is weightless. You feel the shrine notice, and sigh, and let you go.

events.text: The bell of a burned shrine was thrown into a pond, and on still nights you can hear it ringing under the water. A frog sits on the rim of the pond and ribbits in time.

choices.text: Dive for the bell

effects.log: The water is warm. The bell is bigger than you thought and rings softly when you touch it, and you rise holding your breath and a small stolen peace.

choices.text: Sit with the frog and listen

effects.log: Frog and god keep time together. The bell, you suspect, is not displeased.

events.text: On the one standing wall of a burned shrine, a mural has survived: a god with an oar, a god with a loom, and between them, a third figure whose face was scraped away. The scraping is neat and recent.

choices.text: Trace the scraped outline with your hand

effects.log: Under your fingers the wall is warmer where the face was. You feel the shape of a smile.

choices.text: Ask the elder gods who was erased

effects.log: The elders look at their feet. Nobody answers.

events.text: A thurible lies upright in the ash of a burned shrine, still full of incense. It has not burned. It has been waiting for a lighter, and the sticks are fresh as the day they were made.

choices.text: Light it, in whatever name it was meant for

effects.log: The smoke curls up in the shape of a bird, hesitates, and goes away east.

choices.text: Leave it for the next to come

effects.log: The thurible waits. The right visitor, you suspect, will come in time.

events.text: A cat of no particular beauty sleeps on the burned altar of a god no one names. When you bring it a bowl of milk it says, quite plainly, that the god did not like milk, but was fond of cats.

choices.text: Pour a second bowl for the god

effects.log: The cat looks at the second bowl, then at you, and purrs once, as a courtesy.

choices.text: Ask the cat what else the god liked

effects.log: The cat names six small joys and falls asleep halfway through the seventh.

events.text: The ruin of a shrine is covered in the scribbles of passing gods: names, jokes, a curse that someone later crossed out and replaced with a pun. The oldest line is the shortest: we were here.

choices.text: Add: so were we

effects.log: You write it in your own hand. It looks right.

choices.text: Read every line, and remember the best

effects.log: You carry a dozen jokes out of the ruin and feel less alone with the old gods.

events.text: At dusk the wind in a burned valley blows warm, and it carries the faint smell of a feast. If you stand very still you can almost hear a god laughing and a crowd laughing back.

choices.text: Stand and let the feast pass through you

effects.log: For a few breaths you are at the table. Then the wind turns cold, and you are only a god in a valley, with a full heart.

choices.text: Pour a cup into the ash

effects.log: The ash drinks it. The laughter swells for a moment and then slips away.

events.text: The wardens of a sealed heaven give you a small clay token the day you pass the wall for the tenth time. It means you may knock, and it means they will answer. It has never been used.

choices.text: Knock once, politely

effects.log: The wall answers with a knock of its own, a soft old rap. Then silence, and a sense of being considered.

choices.text: Keep the token unused

effects.log: It warms in your pocket. Some tokens are best left as promises.

events.text: A dragonfly of pale gold crosses the seal of a walled heaven as if the wall were a breath of air, and rests on your sleeve. It has been inside; it smells of cold fields and sleep.

choices.text: Hold out your hand and ask what is inside

effects.log: The dragonfly does not answer, but a small scene blooms in your mind: a long meadow under copper light.

choices.text: Let it go

effects.log: It flies back through the seal, and the wall hums once, grateful.

events.text: A ladder leans against nothing in the middle of a burned courtyard. The rungs are blackened, and at the top, someone has hung a small basket. In it are a smooth stone and a note: for the climber.

choices.text: Climb it, rung by rung

effects.log: At the top the ash wind smells of a pine and a bonfire. You touch the sky for a breath, and descend lighter.

choices.text: Leave the basket for another

effects.log: The basket stays. Someone else will want it more.

events.text: Behind a seal of grey iron a choir sings, an old song for a harvest that never came. The wardens say the song has been lowering by a note each century, and they fear what will happen when it reaches the floor.

choices.text: Hum an octave higher to keep it aloft

effects.log: Your voice rides the seal. The choir slides upward, and for a moment the wall rings with a hopeful, rising chord.

choices.text: Ask the wardens to write the song down

effects.log: They agree gravely. The song is now in ink, which will last longer than the throats.

events.text: In the char of a shrine, a pair of bronze scales lies tilted. On one pan sits a small stone; on the other, a lock of hair. Someone has been weighing a debt that no god recorded.

choices.text: Set a pinch of faith on the empty side

effects.log: The scales rock and settle level. The stone and the hair lie quiet, and the debt is, in a way, forgiven.

choices.text: Take the lock of hair back to the nearest river

effects.log: The river takes it, and carries it away with a murmur that sounds like a thank-you.

events.text: A stray beast, thin and grey, has been sleeping against a seal for many winters, warming the stone with its flank. It looks up when you come, with eyes that are not an animal's.

choices.text: Bring it food and a blanket

effects.log: It eats and it sleeps. When you return, the seal is faintly warmer, and the beast is no longer thin.

choices.text: Ask what it hears through the wall

effects.log: It makes a small sound, a lowing, and then a hum. Behind the wall something low and old hums back.

events.text: Half a mask hangs on a nail in the ruin of a shrine: gilt, thin, laughing. The missing half has been found on the far side of the world, in the shrine of a rival, and the two have wanted each other ever since.

choices.text: Carry the mask across the world and join the halves

effects.log: The two halves click into one face, and it sighs. Both shrines seem to unclench a little.

choices.text: Hang it back and say nothing

effects.log: You leave the mask to its nail. A longing is sometimes all a ruin has.

events.text: {npc} is mapping every sealed heaven in the realm, with a measuring cord and a lamp on a pole. {He} says nobody has ever drawn them all, because no god wants to admit how many there are. {He} asks if you will walk one wall with {him}.

choices.text: Walk the wall and hold the cord

effects.log: The wall is longer than it looks. By dusk you have found two doors the wardens never listed.

choices.text: Lend {him} your domain's old charts

effects.log: The charts fit like a missing tooth. {npc} laughs aloud and writes your name in the margin.

choices.text: Wish {him} luck

effects.log: {npc} thanks you gravely and trudges on with the lamp.

events.text: One of the unlisted doors is slightly open. A draught comes out that smells of a kitchen on a feast day. {npc} stares at the gap and, for the first time, does not write anything down.

choices.text: Go in, with {npc} behind you

effects.log: Past the door a long hall stands set for a banquet that never began. Every dish is still hot.

choices.text: Close the door gently and mark it

effects.log: You mark it on the map with a small cross. {npc} sighs, as if relieved of a temptation.

events.text: Your domain's charts show a wall on {npc}'s map that nobody else could see: a heaven sealed from the inside. {He} asks who would seal themselves in.

choices.text: Say it may have been a sanctuary

effects.log: The idea settles on {him} like a shawl. {He} adds a small mark: a hearth.

choices.text: Say you do not know, and that is why you map

effects.log: You say it kindly. {npc} smiles, a long slow smile of a god who loves the question.

events.text: The banquet hall has no guests but a long table of pewter plates, each with a name card. One card is yours. {npc} does not look at it. {He} says gods that are set a place should sit.

choices.text: Sit in your place

effects.log: The dishes steam. A voice at the far end of the table, which you cannot see, says: at last. The table fills with a quiet crowd of the unborn.

choices.text: Leave the place set and pull the door shut

effects.log: You step back. The card fades. {npc} writes beside the door: someone is expected.

events.text: {npc} finishes the map in your old age. It shows eight hundred sealed heavens, and it is beautiful, a whole sky of closed doors. {He} hands you the first copy and says every door is a promise someone made.

choices.text: Hang it in your shrine

effects.log: Worshippers study it and begin, strangely, to pray for the closed doors. Your faith rises in odd ways.

choices.text: Give it to the wardens

effects.log: The wardens treat it like a holy book and start, at last, to visit each other.

events.text: The wall of this sealed heaven has clocks in it, hundreds, all showing the same minute. A warden warns you that nobody who goes in has come out the same age. Some come out younger and some come out never.

choices.text: Go in with your own hour-glass

effects.log: Your hour-glass runs slow at the door, then not at all. Past the gate, the air is thick as honey.

choices.text: Ask the warden what the clocks are for

effects.log: They are not for telling time. They are a lock, and every stopped clock is a stopped hand on the door.

choices.text: Stay outside and read the clocks

effects.log: You read them from the doorway. The same minute, in a hundred hands. A very long moment.

events.text: Inside, a god sits at a long desk with a thousand clocks and one pen. The keeper is winding a clock one tick at a time, to buy back an afternoon from a war nobody won. They look up at you without surprise.

choices.text: Reach for the nearest clock-hand

ok.log: You stay your hand just as the minute turns. The keeper bows to you, relieved.

fail.log: The hand moves under your touch and the gate behind you clicks over by an age.

choices.text: Sit and listen to the keeper

effects.log: The keeper tells you of the afternoon they are buying back. It is a small one, a picnic.

events.text: The warden says the stopped clocks were set by gods who feared an end. If the hands never move, the war never ends, but neither does the peace. They are tired of being the clock's caretaker.

choices.text: Offer to take a shift at the wall

effects.log: For a night you wipe the dust from the clock-hands. It is quiet, grand, strange work.

choices.text: Thank the warden and leave

effects.log: Some tired are best left to rest.

events.text: The keeper is almost done. One afternoon bought back, one tick at a time, and when it comes the picnic lasts exactly as long as a picnic does. Then the clocks, all of them, begin to move.

choices.text: Stay for the picnic

effects.log: You eat bread and plums with a god you will never meet again. The clocks tick, relieved. The heaven opens like a cheerful door.

choices.text: Step out as the clocks start

effects.log: You are out before the first strike. Behind you, the heaven rings with a thousand small bells.

events.text: You step out of the heaven and the sky is a different colour. A warden you do not know says the year, and it is eleven years later. Your shrine has been tended by strangers, and a few of them still remember your name.

choices.text: Thank the strangers

effects.log: They blush and look at the floor. Someone has been telling stories of you, and they are better than the truth.

choices.text: Take up your domain again, quietly

effects.log: You return to the work as if only an afternoon had gone by. It had not.

events.text: The courts have no shrine for a god of no pantheon, so you walk, and in a burned valley you find a ruin no pantheon claims. A roofless hall and an altar. It would not be much, but it would be yours.

choices.text: Claim the ruin and light a single lamp

effects.log: The lamp burns. The ruin hums with surprise. Somewhere a ledger closes on a long unfilled line.

choices.text: Ask the valley's old tenants first

effects.log: A line of crows, a fox, and a snail make slow room for you on the altar-step. The fox yawns approval.

choices.text: Pass it by and keep walking

effects.log: A home that is not asked for is not a home. You walk on.

events.text: A herald of a pantheon arrives with a scroll: the ruin is the property of the Silent Hall and has been for an age. They would like you to leave. You are the third masterless god to try.

choices.text: Argue the law of the empty altar

effects.log: You cite a rule of precedence older than the Hall. The herald is flustered, then fascinated, then gone.

choices.text: Offer the pantheon a share of your faith as rent

effects.log: The herald takes it with pursed lips. You have a lease, and a nervous landlord.

events.text: The valley animals are the first to worship you, and not very well. The fox leaves bones on the altar, the crows leave shiny things. You take it for what it is: a congregation.

choices.text: Teach them proper prayers

effects.log: The fox picks it up fastest. By spring the altar is a lopsided chorus.

choices.text: Accept the bones and shiny things as they are

effects.log: The congregation brightens. Your faith rises by a little, and then by a lot.

events.text: Years pass. The ruin has a roof now, a door and a stoop. Pilgrims arrive, a few at a time, to see the first shrine of a god who owes nobody. A herald brings you an invitation to a court you were never asked to before.

choices.text: Accept, and wear the same plain coat

effects.log: You are seated low at the court feast, but you are seated. The valley animals are jealous.

choices.text: Decline, and keep the valley's hearth warm

effects.log: You send your regrets and a basket of your valley's plums. They are eaten with gusto, and not spoken of.

events.text: The pantheon's claim is called in at last, and you pay the rent of a tenant: a little faith, a lot of grace. The ruin is partly yours and partly theirs, and the fox is partly both.

choices.text: Keep the arrangement

effects.log: You hold the house and the Hall holds the deed. Strange peace, but it is a peace.

choices.text: Buy the deed with a year of hard-won faith

effects.log: You pay in full and the ruin is yours alone. The fox, who understands none of it, brings you a mouse in celebration.

events.text: The seal on a walled heaven has learned to speak. It does not say anything useful. It says good morning, and the weather is coming, and has anyone seen my keys.

choices.text: Answer it politely

effects.log: You say good morning back. The seal considers this, and says: that was kind, and then falls silent for a week.

choices.text: Ask it what it is guarding

effects.log: It does not know. It says it was told to hold, and holding is what it does.

choices.text: Ignore it

effects.log: You pass. The seal says: you too, and the wind carries it.

events.text: Over many visits the seal grows chattier. It tells you what the wardens say when they think no one is listening, and there is a name that keeps coming up: a warden who has been taking small tithes from the wall.

choices.text: Tell the chief warden quietly

effects.log: The chief warden thanks you and deals with it kindly. The seal says: oh good, and you laugh.

choices.text: Say nothing, and ask the seal not to gossip

effects.log: The seal promises, and then tells you three more things. Gossip, it seems, is what it is for.

events.text: The seal says it remembers one thing about what is behind it: a song. It hums three bars of it, wrongly, and again, and then a fourth bar comes from behind the wall, in a voice not its own.

choices.text: Hum the fifth bar

effects.log: The wall answers with a sixth. You trade bars with the thing in the heaven until dark.

choices.text: Write the song down and give it to a bard

effects.log: The bard sings it at a court feast. Three gods weep and cannot say why.

events.text: One morning the seal says goodbye. It says it has been holding for so long that holding has become a kind of loving, and it is ready to be let go. The wall opens a little wider than a door.

choices.text: Thank it and stay with it as it opens

effects.log: It sighs and opens like a flower. What is behind it is a garden, and a very old gardener who nods at you.

choices.text: Ask it to hold a little longer

effects.log: It laughs, a creak of old stone. It holds for another thousand years, but now you are its friend.

events.text: The fifth bar and the sixth are all the song you will ever get, a lullaby cut in half. The seal says it is enough to hold a heaven closed, if the heaven is sleeping, and a lullaby is the only lock it has ever needed.

choices.text: Sing the half-lullaby at the seal each year

effects.log: The seal hums along. The heaven behind it sleeps through the centuries, soft as a held breath.

choices.text: Leave the song with the seal

effects.log: You trust the seal with the song. It, at least, will not forget.

events.text: The shrine of {npc}, a god of a rival pantheon who has snubbed you at three feasts, has burned in the night. The embers are still warm. Nobody has come to see, and {he} is nowhere to be found.

choices.text: Search the ashes for survivors

effects.log: You find a shrine-keeper under a collapsed beam, shaken and angry at the world. You bring the keeper to your own shrine for tea.

choices.text: Look for the cause of the fire

effects.log: The fire began in the lamp-room, at the altar. Not arson. A lamp tipped and nobody was there to right it.

choices.text: Leave it for their own to find

effects.log: Not your quarrel, you tell yourself, and you do not quite believe it.

events.text: {npc} turns up days later, thin and furious, and sees your shrine-keeper at your table. {He} does not thank you. {He} does ask, at last, in a low, ungracious voice, whether the keeper is well.

choices.text: Say the keeper is well, and fed

effects.log: {npc} nods stiffly. It is the most polite thing {he} has ever said to you.

choices.text: Tell {him} a rival does not owe you thanks

effects.log: It is a graceful thing to say and {he} knows it. {He} blinks at you for the first time as if at a person.

events.text: The tipped lamp had a cracked base that anyone could have seen. {npc} will not like being told so. Still, you carry a new lamp to the burned shrine and set it on the altar without a word.

choices.text: Leave the lamp and a note

effects.log: The note says only: yours. {npc} reads it at dawn and keeps the lamp for the rest of {his} life.

choices.text: Leave the lamp and no note

effects.log: It is sweeter without a note. {npc} will guess, and will say nothing, and that will do.

events.text: A year on, {npc} sits beside you at a court feast, in a seat {he} cleared with a cough. It is not friendship. It is two old gods agreeing not to be enemies, which is rarer and nearly as good.

choices.text: Pour {him} a cup

effects.log: {He} accepts with a nod. The court notices, and for once does not gossip.

choices.text: Ask for the rebuilt shrine's first blessing

effects.log: {He} laughs, short and surprised, and blesses you in the old style. It is a good blessing.

events.text: A shrine-keeper of a burned shrine kept the shrine's bell when everything else turned to ash. Each dawn the keeper rings it, three strokes, for a god who might be listening. Today the bell rings four.

choices.text: Ring the fourth stroke for the unnamed

effects.log: The fourth stroke hums longer than the rest. The keeper bows to you, wordless.

choices.text: Ask the keeper who the fourth is for

effects.log: The keeper looks pleased to be asked. A visitor, they say. Possibly you.

events.text: A walled-off heaven hangs a bell over its gate, and the clapper has been tied with a ribbon. A card reads: please do not ring, we are sleeping. Beneath it, in a different hand: but if it is you, ring.

choices.text: Ring it softly

effects.log: The bell gives a note like a held breath. Inside, a long creak, and a dim lantern lights.

choices.text: Retie the ribbon for them

effects.log: You retie the ribbon carefully. A faint sigh of thanks drifts out of the wall.

events.text: Among the black stumps of a burned shrine, one pear tree has blossomed out of season. Its fruit hangs like small lanterns. A tag on the bough reads: the god of pears would like you to eat.

choices.text: Eat one in thanks

effects.log: It is the sweetest pear you have ever tasted. A faint, happy ghost laughs in the branches.

choices.text: Plant a seed in your own domain

effects.log: The seed takes in a corner of your grounds. In ten years the pear god has a new, small, noisy shrine.

events.text: On a seal in the Wall-Ring someone has carved a prayer in nine tongues, and all nine say the same thing: forgive us. The wardens do not know what for, but they dust the carving every week.

choices.text: Add a tenth tongue, yours

effects.log: You carve the line in the old script of your own domain. The stone warms and settles, as if finally satisfied.

choices.text: Ask the wardens to say what they feel

effects.log: They look surprised to be asked. One of them admits to a grief they did not know was there.

events.text: Lanterns drift down the black river from a burned shrine, one for each night the shrine stood. They stop where the river bends. A frog tends them, flicking out the ones that burn too low.

choices.text: Light a lantern of your own for the river

effects.log: It joins the others, small and brave. The frog nods once.

choices.text: Ask the frog how many nights are left

effects.log: Three thousand, the frog says, without turning. Then you will see something.

events.text: The wardens have cut a peephole in a seal, no wider than a coin. You may look, if you pay a small tithe, and they say nobody has ever looked twice.

choices.text: Pay and look

effects.log: You see a single room with a single bed and a single sleeper, breathing steadily. A cat on the pillow opens one eye and shuts it.

choices.text: Decline, and respect the sleeper

effects.log: You respect the sleeper. The warden nods; many do not.

events.text: A burned shrine's kitchen holds a hundred wooden spoons, each carved with a worshipper's name, each blackened at the bowl. One spoon is fresh, and bears the name of nobody anyone knows.

choices.text: Carve your own name on the fresh spoon

effects.log: You carve it, awkwardly. The spoon fits your hand as though it were measured for you.

choices.text: Wash the spoons in the stream

effects.log: The stream carries the soot away, and the names come up clear. A hundred small voices say thank you at once.

events.text: An owl of pale amber perches on the wall of a sealed heaven and hoots in an ancient grammar. When you answer it badly, it corrects you, patiently, and hoots again. It has been teaching the wall to say please.

choices.text: Learn the owl's grammar

effects.log: It takes all night. By dawn you can say please, thank you and not yet in a language older than the domains.

choices.text: Thank the owl and leave it a fish

effects.log: The owl takes the fish with grave dignity and turns back to the wall.

events.text: Children of a nearby valley play in a burned shrine, because the ash is soft and the walls are good for hide-and-seek. A small one asks if the god who lived here minds. You do not know, but you say no.

choices.text: Join the game of hide-and-seek

effects.log: You are found in four breaths by a six-year-old. It is a humbling and cheerful afternoon.

choices.text: Leave them a gift on the altar-step

effects.log: The children find a bowl of honey-cakes and decide the god minds nothing at all.

events.text: A gardener of the walled-off heavens tends the grass on the outside of a seal, because someone has to. The gardener says the grass has a way of growing greener where it is watched.

choices.text: Help trim the grass

effects.log: You spend an afternoon with shears. The seal, you think, enjoys it.

choices.text: Ask what grows on the other side

effects.log: The gardener says: the same thing, but taller, and sadder.

events.text: A wind chime of black ceramic still hangs in the ruin of a burned shrine, and when the wind comes it plays a tune you almost know. It is a hymn for a god of small, ordinary mornings.

choices.text: Hum along

effects.log: The chime and you hum together. The hymn feels like waking in a house you grew up in.

choices.text: Take the chime to your shrine

effects.log: You hang it by the door. At dawn it plays the hymn. Your shrine-keeper hums too.

events.text: A fallen god's vault stands open on a cold plain, doors wide, nothing guarding it. Inside, on a stone desk, a ledger lies open to a column of debts the dead god was owed, and a note: whoever pays one may take one.

choices.text: Read the debts

effects.log: A hundred small debts: a song, a loaf, a promise to visit. Each one is signed by a worshipper.

choices.text: Pick the smallest debt and pay it

effects.log: You pay a debt of one loaf. A drawer in the desk slides open of its own accord.

choices.text: Close the ledger and leave

effects.log: You touch nothing. The vault does not mind; it has waited this long.

events.text: The drawer holds a relic: a small cracked horn on a cord. A card inside says it was used to call worshippers home at dusk. It would work again, if the debt behind it were all paid.

choices.text: Pay a second debt for the horn

effects.log: You pay again, a promise to visit a grave. The horn warms, and the cord shortens to fit your wrist.

choices.text: Leave the horn and pay nothing more

effects.log: The drawer closes. You have done a small good and asked for nothing.

events.text: The debts in the ledger run back many ages. As you read, you see that most were never collected, because the god died first. A worshipper is still waiting, somewhere, for a song that was promised.

choices.text: Seek out the oldest debt's heir

effects.log: You find a grandchild in a hill-hamlet who tells you the song was a lullaby. You sing it, badly, and they weep.

choices.text: Copy the ledger for the wardens of fallen gods

effects.log: The wardens receive it with a murmur. A whole office wakes up that has had nothing to do for centuries.

events.text: You call the dusk home with the horn, and across the plain a faint answering note rises from a hundred small graves. The worshippers of the fallen god hear it, and their descendants look up from their fields without knowing why.

choices.text: Blow the horn each dusk for a year

effects.log: By year's end a ring of shrines has quietly sprouted on the plain. The fallen god has, once more, a flock.

choices.text: Hang the horn in the vault, and shut the door

effects.log: The vault is shut with a click. The ledger sighs, closed at last, and you walk away lighter.

events.text: The grandchild brings a friend, then ten, to learn the lullaby. By summer a school of singers has taken over the vault, and the dead god's ledger becomes a songbook.

choices.text: Teach them the second verse

effects.log: You do. The vault rings. In the rafters, the ghost of a god of lullabies tilts an ear.

choices.text: Let them find it themselves

effects.log: They will. It takes them till autumn. They are prouder of it that way.

events.text: Under a stair of the Silent Hall is a room the Hall does not list: a loom-room of Fate, small, dusty, with a single loom and ten thousand spools. The threads are moving a little, as if in a draught, although there is none.

choices.text: Touch one thread

effects.log: It is warm and humming. You feel, faintly, a stranger's week: a market, a quarrel, a laugh.

choices.text: Look for a record of the room

effects.log: A card on the wall: the threads are drawn by hand from living lives. Please do not tangle. Please do not cut.

choices.text: Step back and close the door

effects.log: You close the door gently. The threads sigh as if relieved to be left alone.

events.text: Following one thread out of the room and into the world, you find the life at the end of it: a ferryman, middle-aged, about to make a mistake that will cost three lives. The thread is thin there, fraying.

choices.text: Mend the thread with a careful knot

ok.log: The knot holds. The ferryman steadies the oar at the last instant and three lives continue.

fail.log: The knot slips. You can only watch.

choices.text: Leave the thread alone

effects.log: Fate, you tell yourself, is not yours to mend. It does not feel like wisdom.

events.text: The card is signed by the Weaver in a small tidy hand. It ends: if you are reading this, you are the third visitor in a thousand years, and I would like to have a word.

choices.text: Wait in the loom-room for the Weaver

effects.log: Unmyeong comes at dusk with a cup of tea and sits on the second stool. Nothing is asked but your name.

choices.text: Take the card to the Hall

effects.log: The Hall peruses it with great gravity and misplaces it by evening.

events.text: The ferryman's thread is whole now, and in the room a new spool of bright gold has appeared, labelled with your name. The Weaver says nothing of it, and hands you a little shuttle to try.

choices.text: Weave a hand's breadth of a stranger's luck

effects.log: It is the most delicate thing you have ever done. The stranger, far away, finds a coin in the street and thinks nothing of it.

choices.text: Decline the shuttle, with thanks

effects.log: A smile, almost approving. Some tools are better left in expert hands.

events.text: The thread frays. Three lives are lost in the river, and the loom-room dims. A card lies on the bench, newly written: it is not your fault; do come back. It is signed, in the tidy hand, with only an initial.

choices.text: Go back, and sit with the loom

effects.log: Fate is not all gold. You learn that the loom keeps even its failures, folded in drawers, and the drawers are never empty.

choices.text: Mourn the three, and move on

effects.log: You light three small lamps in the nearest shrine. It is something.

events.text: Deep in the vault of a fallen god of harvests, {npc} is sorting jars. Each jar holds a prayer that arrived too late, after the god died, still glowing faintly. {He} has been at it for years and says it is the saddest and best work {he} has had.

choices.text: Help {him} sort the jars

effects.log: You sort until your eyes ache. Each prayer is plain: please let the rain come, please let the baby live.

choices.text: Ask {him} what happens to the jars

effects.log: {He} says nothing happens. The prayers keep, forever, waiting for a god to hear them.

choices.text: Admire the jars and leave

effects.log: You stand a while among the glow. Then you go, quieter than you came.

events.text: Among the jars is one that has your name on it. A prayer from a worshipper you never met, long dead, who prayed to you in the hour before you had a domain at all.

choices.text: Open the jar and listen

effects.log: It is a child's prayer, from the day before you were a god: be kind. Your hand trembles.

choices.text: Keep it sealed, and carry it close

effects.log: You tie it to your belt. It warms against you, a small, fierce little ember of someone's trust.

events.text: {npc} explains that a god may answer an unspent prayer, if willing to bear it. The answer lands in the world late, small and strange: a rain that falls on a field long since sold.

choices.text: Answer one prayer, the smallest

effects.log: A rain falls, ten summers late, on a hillside that no one remembers farming. Wildflowers come up, then bees.

choices.text: Decide to answer none

effects.log: It is too heavy to carry. {npc} nods, not unkindly.

events.text: You take the child's prayer to the shrine of a small god of kindness, and read it aloud before the altar. The altar light brightens, and for a breath the whole shrine smells of bread. The jar is empty.

choices.text: Leave the empty jar as an offering

effects.log: The shrine-keeper sets it by the door. Visitors, passing it, always lower their voices.

choices.text: Take the empty jar home

effects.log: It sits on your shelf. Sometimes, when the house is quiet, it hums a note.

events.text: The prayer on your belt warms through the years. By the end of an age it is the only warm thing about you, and a young god, passing, asks if they may hold it. You let them, for a moment.

choices.text: Tell them whose it was

effects.log: They listen to the whole story and cry a little. They leave you a bowl of figs.

choices.text: Say it is a secret

effects.log: They nod. The prayer, you think, enjoys being private.

events.text: A hall of banners, a thousand of them, hangs in the vault of a fallen god of war. Each is a little stiff with age. A draught runs through them that should not be there, and the banners lean towards you as one.

choices.text: Walk the hall slowly

effects.log: The banners rustle as you pass. Each one bears a name, and each name is the name of someone who did not come home.

choices.text: Salute the banners

effects.log: They stop moving, all at once. The hush is exact, military and tender.

choices.text: Retreat to the doorway

effects.log: The banners follow you with their eyes, if banners have eyes.

events.text: At the end of the hall, a banner larger than the rest hangs over a stone chair. A voice, dry as dust, speaks from it: who commands here? It is not a question. It is a test.

choices.text: Answer in the old fighting tongue

ok.log: The banners ripple. The voice grunts approval: well spoken, young one. A path opens to the chair.

fail.log: You stumble over a word. The banners snap taut, and a gust throws you against the wall.

choices.text: Say: none of us, anymore

effects.log: The banners go still. A long silence. Then: honest. The voice rests, the banners fall limp, and the chair is yours to sit in.

events.text: The banners salute you back, the whole thousand of them, with a sound like a flight of doves. One of them detaches, floats down, and folds itself into your hands: a plain white banner with a blank field.

choices.text: Take the white banner

effects.log: It is soft and warm. In time you understand it is the banner of an army that never lost a soul, because it never marched.

choices.text: Return it to the hall

effects.log: It rises and goes home. The salute fades.

events.text: The chair is only a chair. Behind it, a locked chest of the war god's oldest vow: that no soldier should be forgotten. It opens to the touch of one who sat there honestly.

choices.text: Take the vow into your own keeping

effects.log: It settles into your chest like a second heartbeat. The war god is, in a way, with you now.

choices.text: Read the vow aloud and leave it in the hall

effects.log: The banners rustle. A thousand names, finally spoken. They sag, grateful, and the draught stops.

events.text: You are thrown out of the hall, battered but whole. A banner trails after you and slides under your door at night, as if sorry. It carries a name: yours.

choices.text: Keep the banner as a warning

effects.log: It hangs on your wall. A reminder that some halls answer only one kind of person.

choices.text: Send it back with a note of apology

effects.log: The banner returns, and the hall is quiet. A truce, of a kind.

events.text: A vault of a fallen god is kept by a mouse. It sits on the lintel with a tiny brass key, and it asks, in a voice like a pen scratching, whether you are the heir. It has been waiting a very long time and is strict.
events.arc: The Mouse Who Keeps the Vault

choices.text: Say yes, you are the heir

effects.log: The mouse peers at you, whiskers working. It does not believe you, but it is polite.

choices.text: Say no, and ask for tea

effects.log: The mouse is delighted. It has not been asked for tea in four thousand years.

choices.text: Bow to the mouse

effects.log: The mouse bows back, a dignified, swift dip.

events.text: The mouse tests the claim of heirship with three questions: the god's favourite colour, the name of the god's dog, the hour of the god's death. You know none of them.
events.arc: The Mouse Who Keeps the Vault

choices.text: Guess from what you have seen of the vault

ok.log: Green, Hound, dusk. The mouse squeaks, astonished, and lets you in.

fail.log: Blue, Rex, midnight. The mouse sighs and turns away, tail flicking.

choices.text: Admit you do not know

effects.log: The mouse thinks the honesty is a seventh answer. It nods, and lets you in.

events.text: Over tea, the mouse tells you about the god: a god of small kindnesses who died of a cold, with the mouse on the shoulder. The mouse has been guarding a jar of sneezes ever since.
events.arc: The Mouse Who Keeps the Vault

choices.text: Ask to see the jar

effects.log: It is a jam-jar with a cork. The mouse lifts the lid a hair and an ancient sneeze escapes, comic and sad.

choices.text: Offer the mouse a place at your shrine

effects.log: The mouse thinks for a long time. It accepts, but only on the lintel.

events.text: Past the door is a single warm room, with a bed, a chair and a mug still on the table. The mouse tells you the vault holds no treasure. It holds a home, and the mouse is its caretaker.
events.arc: The Mouse Who Keeps the Vault

choices.text: Sit in the chair for a moment

effects.log: The chair fits you. The mouse, on the table, tells you the god's last joke. You laugh until you cry.

choices.text: Make the bed and wash the mug

effects.log: The mouse watches with approval. The room looks lived in for the first time in an age.

events.text: The mouse closes the door on you, politely. As you leave, you hear it begin its night rounds. You return a year later with a good cheese. The door opens at once.
events.arc: The Mouse Who Keeps the Vault

choices.text: Leave the cheese on the doorstep

effects.log: The mouse takes it and says nothing. The next morning there is a tiny bell on your door.

choices.text: Eat the cheese yourself, on the steps

effects.log: The mouse watches from the lintel. In the end it shares a crumb.

events.text: In an abandoned loom-room, a pair of silver shears lies on the bench beside a thread running up into the dark. The thread is thick and golden, and it hums with a life that is very, very near its end.

choices.text: Follow the thread up

effects.log: It leads up a stair into a cold gallery, where a figure lies asleep at the end of it, breathing slowly.

choices.text: Take the shears and put them away

effects.log: You hide them in a drawer. The thread hums a little less urgently.

choices.text: Leave the room

effects.log: You leave. The thread stays, and the shears stay, and it all stays unmade.

events.text: The sleeper is a god of an old pantheon, tired past waking. The thread is their life, and the shears were left by a friend who could not bear to see them suffer. The god opens one eye and asks you to decide.

choices.text: Mend the thread so they may sleep longer

ok.log: The thread thickens. The god sighs and closes their eye, and sleeps on.

fail.log: The thread slips between your fingers and snaps. The god smiles, and is gone.

choices.text: Sit with them until the end, unasked

effects.log: You hold their hand. The thread lets go in its own time. They say thank you, and then a name that is not yours.

events.text: A drawer holds a letter in the handwriting of the god who left the shears. It asks the finder to decide for them, because they could not. It is wet with old tears.

choices.text: Return the shears to the loom, uncut

effects.log: You hang them on their nail. The thread, you are sure, settles into sleep.

choices.text: Take the letter to the Hall

effects.log: The Hall receives it. A kindly archivist reads it twice and takes it away to be kept.

events.text: Weeks later the old god wakes, weak and hungry, and finds you at the bedside. They ask for broth. They say it was a long dream, and in it a patient hand held a thread together.

choices.text: Bring the broth and sit with them

effects.log: You are no healer, but you bring broth. They finish the bowl and ask for another. The room fills with sun.

choices.text: Send a healer god from the Green Assembly

effects.log: The healer arrives within the day. The old god is cared for, and you are thanked in a whisper.

events.text: The thread is gone, and the god with it. In the gallery, a small gold knot remains on the pillow, warm, and a blessing: for the one who came. It is the thing you take home, and it never grows cold.

choices.text: Keep the knot at your shrine

effects.log: It hangs by the door, and visitors always lower their voices. Faith, sometimes, comes from quiet things.

choices.text: Bury it under a tree

effects.log: You plant a young pear over it. It will grow for ten thousand years, perhaps.

events.text: A court auction of relics from a fallen god's vault is announced, and nobody quite likes it. The relics are the god's own: a comb, a bowl, a lamp. The auctioneer, a smiling god of the third bell, says the proceeds will build a hall.

choices.text: Attend, and bid for the comb

effects.log: The comb is plain. You win it for a modest tithe. The auctioneer is disappointed.

choices.text: Attend and object quietly

effects.log: You raise a hand to ask where the relics came from. The room goes silent and the auctioneer pales.

choices.text: Stay away

effects.log: You do not go. The auction goes on without you, and without a conscience.

events.text: The comb, when brushed through your hair, whispers. It remembers the god who owned it, and it is angry about being sold. It asks you to take it somewhere kind.

choices.text: Take it to the god's old worshippers

effects.log: You find them in a mountain hamlet. They weep, and set the comb on a high shelf.

choices.text: Keep it, and treat it with care

effects.log: The comb quietens at your shrine. It sings a soft old tune at night, which pleases your shrine-keeper.

events.text: The auctioneer, cornered, admits the relics were stolen. The court is in uproar. A vote is called on what to do, and the vote hangs on a single seat: yours.

choices.text: Vote to return the relics

effects.log: The vote carries by one. The relics go home, the auctioneer is quietly retired, and you feel taller.

choices.text: Abstain, and say you are not sure

effects.log: Abstaining is a choice. The relics are sold, and you are the god who did nothing.

events.text: Years later a plain gift arrives at your shrine: a bowl, a lamp, and a note. The fallen god's worshippers send their thanks. The bowl is warm. The lamp lights itself.

choices.text: Keep the bowl and lamp at your shrine

effects.log: They sit in a quiet corner. Visitors who touch them go out softer.

choices.text: Send them back with a gift of your own

effects.log: Gifts cross the world and back. The bond lasts for ages.

events.text: The comb sings one winter night a song nobody knew, and a god you have never met knocks at the shrine, an old god of the comb's old owner's pantheon, crying. They have heard it from a thousand miles.

choices.text: Let them take the comb

effects.log: They hold it to their chest and say nothing. They leave a seed in a pouch on the step.

choices.text: Invite them to sit and hear the whole song

effects.log: You listen together. At dawn they thank you in the old tongue.

events.text: In a loom-room of Fate, {npc} is on {his} knees amid a knot of threads. Two lives have been tied together by an apprentice's slip: a baker and a sailor, who will now never be happy apart and never meet. {He} asks if you have thin hands.

choices.text: Offer to help untie them

effects.log: Your hands are steady. For an hour the two of you work at the knot, which does not want to come undone.

choices.text: Suggest leaving them tied, just to see

effects.log: It is an odd thought. {npc} looks scandalised and curious at once.

choices.text: Wish {him} luck and go

effects.log: You leave {him} to the knot. It is not your thread.

events.text: The knot gives, a little. Behind it the two lives pull apart, then tug back toward each other, like magnets. {npc} looks at you in despair: they will not stay apart.

choices.text: Tie them again, loosely, as a bow

effects.log: A neat bow. The two lives drift together and apart with the rhythm of a tide.

choices.text: Cut one thread short

effects.log: It would work. It would also take years from the sailor. {npc} stays your hand.

events.text: Left tied, the baker and the sailor find each other in a market at dusk by accident, and quarrel over a loaf. {npc} watches through the threads with a hand over {his} mouth, and laughs.

choices.text: Nudge the sailor's luck a little

effects.log: The sailor drops a coin; the baker returns it. It is a first, small gift.

choices.text: Let it run its course

effects.log: You watch the quarrel soften through the threads. Some things are not for gods to arrange.

events.text: Years pass. The bow in the threads has held. The baker and the sailor keep a bakery by the harbour, and the loaves are called Knot-bread. {npc} brings you a basket, shy, and says they were never untied, only retied well.

choices.text: Eat a loaf, and write the apprentice a good word

effects.log: The apprentice is let off with a laugh. {npc} stays at the loom, a little bolder.

choices.text: Share the loaf with the Weaver

effects.log: Unmyeong tastes it and says nothing, and then takes a second slice. A blessing follows you home.

events.text: The cut thread leaves the sailor short of years, and the baker alone. {npc} does not forgive the lapse, or you. {He} leaves the loom, and the room is quieter for it.

choices.text: Seek {him} out and apologise

effects.log: You find {him} in a garden, pruning. {He} accepts the apology without turning, and goes on pruning.

choices.text: Let {him} go

effects.log: You do not follow. The cost of an easy answer is paid in other coin.

events.text: The loom-room's windows are thick with pale moths that feed on stale fate. A moth lands on your sleeve and pokes it, interested. The Weaver's apprentice says they are harmless, and also that they are never wrong.

choices.text: Follow the moth

effects.log: It leads you through three corridors to a drawer. In the drawer is a thread of a life that was never lived.

choices.text: Brush it off gently

effects.log: It flutters up and away, offended. The other moths turn away from you in unison.

choices.text: Admire the moths

effects.log: They settle on your shoulders, a dozen of them, soft as breath.

events.text: The unlived thread is bright and bare. It is the life of someone who was meant to be, and wasn't. The moths hover around it in a ring. One lands on your hand and waits.

choices.text: Spin the thread a little and give it a start

effects.log: The thread twitches. Somewhere a child you will never meet is born, healthy and loud.

choices.text: Let it rest in the drawer

effects.log: The moths settle. Some lives are best left unspun.

events.text: The offended moths do not forget. For a year a pale cloud follows you, eating the corners of your robes and your minor plans. At last you apologise, aloud, to a moth. It forgives you.

choices.text: Bring the moths a lamp at the loom-room door

effects.log: The moths drift into the light and the pestering stops. They look, you think, a little pleased.

choices.text: Wait out their sulk

effects.log: They lose interest by winter. You lose a sleeve.

events.text: The unlived child grows up, in a hill-town, unremarkable, loved. When they are old, a moth sits on the window-sill of their house at the last, and then flies away with something small, to the loom-room, and the thread is complete.

choices.text: Place a lamp for them at the loom-room

effects.log: The lamp burns on the sill. The moths gather round, and the Weaver, passing, lays a hand on your shoulder.

choices.text: Tell no one, ever

effects.log: It is yours to keep. The moths agree.

events.text: The drawer of unlived lives holds ten thousand threads, all waiting. You come to visit at times and the moths know your step. They bring you, one night, a thread that is about to be lived, and ask you to be the first to know.

choices.text: Wish the life well

effects.log: You murmur it. The moth takes the wish away on its wings like pollen.

choices.text: Thank the moths and leave quietly

effects.log: They return to their ring, content.

events.text: The door of a fallen god's vault has a knocker shaped like a laughing mouth. When you knock, it says: no one home. Then, after a moment: ha. Then, in a smaller voice: please come in.

choices.text: Laugh, and go in

effects.log: The door swings wide, pleased. Inside, a modest, cheerful room of small relics.

choices.text: Ask the knocker its name

effects.log: It tells you, with relief. It has been the door of a funny god for a long time.

events.text: In a glass case in a vault lies the tooth of a fallen god of the hearth. A label says it is the last of their body. A mouse has chewed a very small hole in the case and is staring at it with longing.

choices.text: Shoo the mouse and mend the case

effects.log: The mouse looks wounded. You leave it a crumb of cheese; its pride recovers.

choices.text: Hold the tooth up to the lamp

effects.log: It is warm as a coal. In its heart a small flame turns, still, and the mouse sighs.

events.text: A mirror in a fallen god's vault shows not your face but the face of whoever last looked into it. It is the god themselves, mid-laugh. The mirror seems to have kept the moment, out of kindness.

choices.text: Laugh back at the mirror

effects.log: The god in the glass laughs wider. For a moment you share the joke.

choices.text: Cover the mirror with a cloth

effects.log: You cover it gently. Let the laugh be the last thing it keeps.

events.text: The dust in a long-sealed vault is drifting in a pattern: it forms a hand, then a face, then a word. The word is thank you. The dust sinks to the floor, quite spent.

choices.text: Sweep it into a jar

effects.log: You keep it on a shelf. A little sacred dust is good for a shrine.

choices.text: Leave it where it fell

effects.log: The dust settles. It has said what it came to say.

events.text: In the vault of a fallen god of beasts lies a hunting-horn carved from a single tusk. When you put it to your lips, the beasts of every domain look up for a heartbeat, listening for a call that has not come in an age.

choices.text: Blow one soft note

effects.log: The note rolls out over the realm. Somewhere a hound lifts its head, and puts it down again, content.

choices.text: Set the horn down unplayed

effects.log: You leave it. Some calls are not yours to make.

events.text: A pair of gloves lies folded on the sill of a fallen god's vault, one for each hand of a god who smithed the stars. They are much too big and smell faintly of iron and apple. A note: for the next smith.

choices.text: Try one on

effects.log: It swallows your arm. For a moment you feel the heat of a forge you have never seen.

choices.text: Pass them to a smith god you know

effects.log: The smith god weeps at the gift and gives you a nail of true iron in return.

events.text: In a loom-room the threads hum in chorus, all slightly off key. A small god of the third spool says the loom needs a tuning, which only a visiting god can give, because the loom has forgotten its own sound.

choices.text: Hum the right note

effects.log: The loom steadies and the room warms. The little god smiles.

choices.text: Offer a drop of your faith to the loom

effects.log: A bright thread curls out from your hand and joins the weave.

events.text: A spindle in the loom-room spins by itself and never tires. The apprentice says it is a retired spindle of the first weaver, too stubborn to stop. It spins faster as you watch, hoping for applause.

choices.text: Applaud the spindle

effects.log: It spins in a golden blur and leaves a thread, quite unasked, of pure joy. The apprentice gives it to you.

choices.text: Ask it to rest

effects.log: It slows, grumbling. The apprentice thanks you; it has not stopped in ages.

events.text: A thread in the loom-room is fraying in front of you, gently, fibre by fibre. The apprentice says it belongs to a river-god nobody prays to. It will not last the season unless someone does.

choices.text: Say a prayer to the river-god

effects.log: The thread brightens a little, and the apprentice lets out a breath.

choices.text: Ask where the river-god's shrine is

effects.log: A tiny, forgotten shrine on a dry bank. You promise to visit.

events.text: The dye-vat of the loom-room is a deep blue that smells of old rain. A sign says: every thread dipped here remembers a sorrow. The dyer, a god of small tides, asks if you would like a skein for yourself.

choices.text: Take a skein of the sorrow

effects.log: It sits heavy and soft in your hands. Tonight you will carry one more grief gently.

choices.text: Decline, and thank the dyer

effects.log: The dyer nods. Not everyone is ready for the colour.

events.text: A cat sleeps on the Weaver's cushion in the loom-room, upon a heap of finished fates. It stirs, yawns and knocks a spool over. Somewhere below, three strangers have a surprisingly lucky afternoon.

choices.text: Rescue the spool and return it

effects.log: The cat watches, unrepentant. The luck is yours to place well.

choices.text: Let the cat have its way

effects.log: The cat purrs. Chaos is a god of its own and well fed.

events.text: The loom-room keeps a ledger of every cut thread. It is a thin book. The apprentice shows you the name on the latest line and asks, shyly, if you know a prayer for the dead who were not mourned.

choices.text: Say the prayer you know

effects.log: The apprentice repeats it, word for word, and writes it on the page.

choices.text: Offer to sit a vigil with the ledger

effects.log: You sit till dawn, reading names. The apprentice sleeps on your shoulder.

events.text: The stairs down into a fallen god's vault are worn into dips by the feet of devotees. The dips are in the shape of kneeling. You find, with a small shock, that your knees fit them.

choices.text: Kneel in the dips and listen

effects.log: The stone is cool and patient. Faint under your knees is the pulse of a vanished crowd.

choices.text: Step over them with care

effects.log: You walk on the sides. Some places are best treated like a church.

events.text: A key hangs on a nail in an empty vault. It opens nothing here. The tag, in a careful hand, says: it opens a door in another vault, that I never found. If you find it, please tell me.

choices.text: Take the key and search

effects.log: You will find the door in time. The key is a long errand, warm in your pocket.

choices.text: Leave the key for the next to try

effects.log: The nail hums softly as you step away.

events.text: The vault of a fallen god of orchards has a roof of earth and a garden on top, where the trees still bear. A bee-keeper god tends the hives. They offer you honey and ask about the weather in your domain.

choices.text: Share the honey and the weather

effects.log: You talk till dusk. The bee-keeper is fond of gossip, and the honey is dark and sweet.

choices.text: Buy a hive for your shrine, with faith

effects.log: The bee-keeper gives you a hive for a kind word. Your shrine hums with bees.

events.text: A small river runs through a fallen god's vault, carrying lamps downstream. At the lower door a shrine-keeper catches them with a net, one by one, and relights the ones that have gone out.

choices.text: Help catch the lamps

effects.log: You spend a night at the net. At dawn the lamps float out into the world, bright.

choices.text: Ask whose lamps they are

effects.log: The keeper does not know. They are everyone's, it says, who never had a lamp of their own.

events.text: In the vault of a god of feasts, a long table is still laid, and from nowhere comes the sound of faint, easy laughter. A single plate is empty. A chair is pulled out for you.

choices.text: Sit and eat

effects.log: The food is cold but the company is warm. For an hour you are among friends who are no longer there.

choices.text: Raise a cup to the empty chairs

effects.log: The laughter rises, kind and pleased.

events.text: A fish of silver scales swims lazily through the air of a vault and nibbles at the dust. A nameplate on its tank, now empty, says: for the god who never forgets to feed me. You are, you realise, late.

choices.text: Apologise and feed it

effects.log: The fish forgives with a flick of the tail. It follows you out, trailing a long silver shimmer.

choices.text: Ask the fish whose it was

effects.log: It tells you in small bubbles. A god of one pond. They are missed, still.

events.text: A cradle in a fallen god's vault rocks softly of its own accord. It holds nothing, but there is a dent in the blanket, a small round one. A song plays, once, from the wood.

choices.text: Rock it gently

effects.log: The cradle settles. The dent in the blanket shifts, as if someone turned over.

choices.text: Cover the dent with a warm cloth

effects.log: You tuck it in. The vault feels, for a moment, like a home.

events.text: A vault of a fallen god of clocks has a hundred small chimes, and one is always a note flat. A repairman god, in the corner, says it is the god's own joke and that they are not allowed to fix it.

choices.text: Leave the chime flat

effects.log: You leave it. The vault is more itself that way.

choices.text: Ask the repairman to show you the joke

effects.log: It takes an afternoon. You laugh at the end; the repairman has been waiting for someone to.

events.text: The colours of the loom-room threads are not the colours of the world. One is the exact shade of a held breath. Another is the colour a word has just before it is said. The apprentice teaches you to name them.

choices.text: Learn five colours

effects.log: By dusk you can see the colour of a promise. It is a surprise; it is mostly grey.

choices.text: Ask for the colour of luck

effects.log: The apprentice gives you a pinch of it. You carry it home in a folded leaf.

events.text: At the bottom of the Sea domain, in the dim green silt, stands a shrine nobody remembers building: pillars furred with weed, a bell tied with kelp. The tide-oxen graze around it, and they will not cross its doorstep.

choices.text: Cross the doorstep alone

effects.log: Inside, the water is still and cold. A single lamp burns on the altar, fed by nothing.

choices.text: Ask the oldest ox why it will not go in

effects.log: The ox lows a slow, deep note. Something in the tone says: it is not ours to enter.

choices.text: Admire the pillars from outside

effects.log: The pillars are carved with fish and moons. You leave them untouched.

events.text: On the altar is a conch the size of a cradle. When you lift it, you hear a sea-god's last sermon: not of fear or glory, but of a request. Keep the lamp lit.

choices.text: Light the lamp with your own breath

effects.log: The lamp strengthens. Deep below, a long sigh runs through the silt.

choices.text: Set the conch back and leave it

effects.log: You set it down as you found it. The lamp does not flicker.
