events.text: The oldest ox leads you round the back of the shrine, to a stone with a name cut in it: the sea-god who drowned the shrine themselves, rather than let it be taken. The oxen guard it still.

choices.text: Pour out a measure of your faith for them

effects.log: The silt hums. The oxen lift their heads together and low once in thanks.

choices.text: Sit with the oxen a while

effects.log: They accept you into the herd. For an afternoon you are just another slow, patient beast.

events.text: Each year on the day of the drowning, the oxen gather at the shrine, and the lamp brightens. Now you are among them. Haeryong, Keeper of Tides, sends a grave nod across the waters: someone remembered.

choices.text: Take on the keeping of the lamp

effects.log: You take the lamp on, and the shrine, and its small flock of oxen. It is a quiet, heavy honour.

choices.text: Ask Haeryong to appoint a keeper from the Sea court

effects.log: A young tide-priest arrives and takes the lamp. You visit every spring, as a guest.

events.text: The lamp burns for you each time you pass. The oxen know your step. You never learn the drowned god's name, but the sea does: a small current curls around your ankles, warm, and then lets go.

choices.text: Thank the current

effects.log: You say thank you into the water. Fish rise around you in a bright curious ring.

choices.text: Leave a shell on the doorstep

effects.log: It stays there a hundred years. You never visit again, but it is kept.

events.text: A pearl the size of a fist rolls out of a cleft in the sea-floor and stops at your feet. When you touch it, you remember a day you never lived: a figure at a shoreline, waving at a ship, with a child on the hip.

choices.text: Hold it until the memory ends

effects.log: It ends at dusk with a goodbye. The child is grown and you are crying, and you do not know why.

choices.text: Ask a sea-priest whose it was

effects.log: The priest turns the pearl in the lamplight. It is a parent's, they say; the ship never returned.

choices.text: Roll it back into the cleft

effects.log: It rolls home. You feel a pang of loss, quickly forgotten.

events.text: Holding the pearl, you find yourself walking the sea-floor toward the shoreline from the memory. It is a real place: a cove with a single house, where an old fisher is hanging out nets, who looks at you as if they know you.

choices.text: Give them the pearl

effects.log: The old fisher takes it in both hands and says nothing. Then: that was a good boy. It is all they say.

choices.text: Ask what became of the ship

effects.log: The answer is plain: a storm, and a long wait. The old fisher cannot say whether the sea is kind or cruel, and keeps hanging nets.

events.text: The priest, kind and tired, says gods are asked every year to return pearls like this to the shore, and few do. It is a heavy errand, for it means looking mourners in the face.

choices.text: Take the errand

effects.log: You carry the pearl up the coast. It takes three days, a ferry and a very bad meal.

choices.text: Leave it to the priest

effects.log: The priest accepts the burden with a small bow.

events.text: Seasons on, a fisher leaves a sea-bass on your shrine step each morning, and says nothing. You never learn who sent them, but the old fisher's house has a lamp in the window every night.

choices.text: Leave a lamp of your own in return

effects.log: Two lamps now burn along that coast. Sailors use them as marks.

choices.text: Eat the bass and say a prayer

effects.log: It is delicious. The prayer is for the ship, long overdue.

events.text: The old fisher tells you, with great precision, how to hang a net. The pearl, you are told, is not a memory but a promise: those who die at sea are not lost, only late. You leave the cove a little more at peace.

choices.text: Promise to keep an eye on the cove

effects.log: You do. Storms turn aside from that cove for the rest of the old fisher's life.

choices.text: Thank the fisher and walk on

effects.log: The lesson sits in you. Nets, you think, are a kind of prayer.

events.text: Beneath the Sea domain runs a dark current that carries the dead to Baekun's ferry. It is drawn by eels, long and pale, with lanterns in their mouths. One of them has stopped, mid-current, and will not move.
events.arc: The Ferry-Eels of the Dark Current

choices.text: Swim to the stuck eel

effects.log: The eel looks at you with enormous patience. A rope of kelp has caught its fin.

choices.text: Fetch the ferryman's boy

effects.log: The boy comes, small and solemn, and says nobody has stopped the line in a thousand years.

choices.text: Wait and watch

effects.log: The line of eels grows behind the stuck one, restless. The lanterns flicker.

events.text: Behind the eel, a long line of the dead waits quietly on the current, none complaining. They do not know it has stopped. They think this is how the journey is.
events.arc: The Ferry-Eels of the Dark Current

choices.text: Cut the kelp from the fin

ok.log: The rope parts. The eel shakes itself, nods at you and sets off with the whole line behind it.

fail.log: The rope tightens round your wrist. You get free but the eel writhes in panic.

choices.text: Calm the dead first, and then the eel

effects.log: You tell the dead the truth gently. A hush falls. The eel, hearing it, stops struggling on its own.

events.text: The boy and you work together, and the boy tells you what it is to be a ferryman's apprentice: counting the dead at every crossing, so none is lost. The count stands at nine million, and nobody is tired.
events.arc: The Ferry-Eels of the Dark Current

choices.text: Count with the boy for an hour

effects.log: You count five hundred and forty. The boy thanks you for the company and does not stop.

choices.text: Ask the boy what the dead say

effects.log: A shrug. Mostly thank you. Sometimes: is it far. The answer is always: not very.

events.text: The line starts again. Baekun comes down the current in the long boat, and bows to you, the first bow a ferryman has given a living god. The dead were not harmed, Baekun says quietly, as if it were enormous.
events.arc: The Ferry-Eels of the Dark Current

choices.text: Offer to pole the boat a mile

effects.log: You pole a long, dark mile in silence. The dead are not afraid. At the end Baekun takes the pole back with a nod.

choices.text: Thank Baekun for the courtesy and withdraw

effects.log: You step away. Baekun's boat glides on, a lantern in its prow.

events.text: The eel, rope-burned, limps on. You hold your breath as it passes, and one of the dead whispers thanks. It is not the rope that hurt, it is the fear. You sit in the dark current for a long while.
events.arc: The Ferry-Eels of the Dark Current

choices.text: Sit with the next line of the dead

effects.log: You stay and ease them across, one by one, until the lanterns steady.

choices.text: Return home and rest

effects.log: You rest. Some nights the dark current still sings to you.

events.text: On the sea-floor stands a library whose books are bells. {npc} is the librarian, a patient sea-god with kelp in {his} beard. {He} says each bell holds a whale-song that is not sung any more, and asks whether you have a good ear.

choices.text: Ring a bell and listen

effects.log: It rings a great slow chord that you feel in your ribs. {npc} watches your face with quiet pleasure.

choices.text: Ask what the oldest song is about

effects.log: {He} says it is a lullaby. Whales have sung it to their dead for ten thousand years.

choices.text: Admire the shelves

effects.log: The bells hang in orderly rows, each with a small brass label. You walk the aisles on your toes.

events.text: {npc} shows you the quietest bell. It has not been rung since the last whale who knew its song died. {He} would like it to be sung again, and asks if you will learn it.

choices.text: Learn the song by ear

ok.log: You catch it on the third try. The bell hums back, as if relieved.

fail.log: You get the first phrase and lose the rest. {npc} pats your shoulder, kind.

choices.text: Offer to record it in verse

effects.log: You write it as a poem. It is not the song, but it is close, and {npc} nods.

events.text: The lullaby, {npc} says, is for the dead who have no one. A whale does not sing it for kin; it sings it for strangers. It is a sea habit, and one that gods might copy.

choices.text: Sing it for the stranger in the next grave

effects.log: On a drowned coast you sing it, flat and soft, over an unmarked cairn.

choices.text: Teach it to the sea-priests

effects.log: They learn it by autumn. By winter, the whole coast sings it.

events.text: You sing the lullaby in the library, alone, and the quiet bell answers, and then one beside it, and then the whole room. {npc} sits down on the floor with a hand over {his} eyes. The whales, far out, lift their heads.

choices.text: Sing it again, for them

effects.log: The whales answer from the far dark. It is the first time in ten thousand years the song has been sung back.

choices.text: Stop, and let the room hum

effects.log: The bells hum on without you. Sometimes it is enough to start.

events.text: {npc} writes your poem into a ledger, as a bell is hung next to the quiet one: a bell for the verse. It does not ring true to the old note, but the library, {he} says, has room for more than one kind of memory.

choices.text: Sign the ledger

effects.log: Your name joins a column of a thousand. It is humbling, and a little funny.

choices.text: Decline to sign, and leave a shell

effects.log: The shell is placed on the shelf beside the bell. {npc} is touched.

events.text: In the deepest trench of the Sea domain, below where light is a rumour, there is a door. It is shut with a ring of tide-iron, and the ring has been polished to a shine by something that visits every day.

choices.text: Examine the ring

effects.log: The tide-iron is cold and slightly greasy. It has been handled with great devotion.

choices.text: Wait to see who visits

effects.log: A huge, soft shape comes out of the dark and nuzzles the ring. It is a blind whale, old beyond reckoning.

choices.text: Rise from the trench at once

effects.log: You rise, ears popping. The door stays shut.

events.text: The ring turns easily in your hand. Beyond the door, a cold, dry chamber holds a single bed of kelp and a body wrapped in cloth: a drowned god, asleep, as if put to bed by loving hands.

choices.text: Wake them gently

ok.log: They stir, and a breath of fresh air fills the chamber. The whale outside hums.

fail.log: The cloth crumbles. The sleeper breathes in once, long and deep, and the door slams behind you.

choices.text: Pull the cloth to their chin, and go

effects.log: Respect, you decide, is a form of not waking. The door closes quietly.

events.text: The blind whale takes a liking to you. It guides you around the trench, past a field of glowing sponges, and shows you the door from the other side: a plain archway with a bed beyond it, and the whale's long vigil.

choices.text: Keep it company for a night

effects.log: The whale hums. You hum back. The dark is not the dark, tonight.

choices.text: Leave it a gift of sea-lanterns

effects.log: The whale blinks slowly. Blind or not, it sees the light.

events.text: The sleeper wakes. They say they were put to bed by a friend, long ago, because the world was too loud to bear. They would like to sleep a little longer, but are glad someone came to check. They give you a pearl as a token.

choices.text: Tuck them back in and promise to visit

effects.log: You promise. The whale hums its approval. You visit each year, and always bring something to read aloud.

choices.text: Take the sleeper to the surface

effects.log: They are blinded by the sun and delighted by it. They have forgotten about seagulls.

events.text: The door has locked behind you with the sleeper's long breath. You are in the dry chamber, in the dark, with a god who is not quite awake. The whale sings outside. It takes you three days to find the door again, and you do.

choices.text: Climb out and thank the whale

effects.log: The whale hums. It carries you part of the way up, a huge, silent escort.

choices.text: Rest, and rise at your own pace

effects.log: You rise by stages, slowly. The pressure is a teacher.

events.text: In your sleep, you walk a path of silver grass under no moon. A signpost at a fork reads, in a sleepy hand, to the left: what you wanted. To the right: what you needed. Nothing says which is which.

choices.text: Take the left fork

effects.log: The path winds down into a sunlit room you have been wanting all your life, a quiet place with a window.

choices.text: Take the right fork

effects.log: The path winds up into a cold hill where a figure waits for you with a heavy cloak.

choices.text: Stand at the fork and think

effects.log: You think for what feels like a year. The silver grass waves, patient.

events.text: The sunlit room is exactly what you wanted. A table laid for one, a book, a window that opens on a field you love. The longer you stay, the harder it is to remember anything else.

choices.text: Remember what you left behind

ok.log: You think of your shrine, your worshippers, a half-built bridge. The room dims, and you wake.

fail.log: The room is so warm. You sleep for three days in the waking world, and a shrine goes unattended.

choices.text: Eat a little, read a page, and leave

effects.log: You allow yourself an hour. The room understands and lets you go gently.

events.text: The figure in the cloak gives you a heavy gift: a stone with a name carved on it, a name you have been avoiding. It is a debt, a person, a task. The figure says nothing more.

choices.text: Take the stone, and carry it

effects.log: It is heavy and warm. When you wake it is in your palm, and the name is clear.

choices.text: Leave the stone on the hill

effects.log: You walk down. The figure watches, unreproachful.

events.text: Mongsa the Sleeper turns over in their endless sleep, and a tremor passes through the path. A voice, drowsy and far away, says: both forks go to the same place. You are the one who carries what you wanted and what you needed.

choices.text: Answer: I know

effects.log: The voice chuckles, deep and slow. The path grows brighter, silver, then gold.

choices.text: Ask what that place is

effects.log: The voice says: where you wake. It says nothing more, and the grass whispers closed.

events.text: You wake after the lost days, and your shrine-keeper looks at you with grave eyes. Nothing has gone badly, only quietly wrong: a missed prayer, a candle gone out. You mend what you can.

choices.text: Apologise to the shrine-keeper

effects.log: The keeper bows and brings tea. Nothing more is said, and everything is forgiven.

choices.text: Work twice as hard for a season

effects.log: You do. The shrine recovers, and so does your name.

events.text: In a dream-path of Mongsa you meet {npc}, who is awake. {He} says that is rare, and that {he} walks the paths for a living, delivering small dreams to people who have none. Business, {he} says, is slow.

choices.text: Ask {him} to deliver one to you

effects.log: {npc} reaches into a satchel and hands you a dream of a cool cellar and a jar of honey. You carry it out of sleep.

choices.text: Offer to help carry the satchel

effects.log: {He} gives you the lighter half. The two of you walk the silver paths, handing dreams to the sleeping.

choices.text: Wish {him} good trade

effects.log: {npc} laughs and tips an invisible hat.

events.text: {npc} shows you a stall of lost dreams in a hollow of the path: dreams nobody collected, dreams that went stale, dreams that are really nightmares in costume. {He} says to touch none of them.

choices.text: Pick one up anyway

ok.log: It is a dream of a sunlit road. You carry it out of sleep and it gives you a week of easy mornings.

fail.log: It is a nightmare in costume. You wake sweating and unable to sleep for three days.

choices.text: Leave the dreams where they are

effects.log: You leave them in their cart. They hum behind you, resentful.

events.text: Your delivered dream does a strange thing: it comes back. A week later, {npc} meets you in a corridor of sleep, anxious. The dream was meant for someone else, and now that someone has dreamt twice. {He} asks if you will explain.

choices.text: Go to the dreamer, in sleep

effects.log: You find them, a tired parent with a small child. You tell the truth, kindly. The dream is taken with a smile.

choices.text: Ask {npc} to handle it

effects.log: {He} does, with a little blush. The mix-up becomes a story {he} tells for years.

events.text: {npc} gives you a gift at last, the first satchel {he} ever carried: small, frayed, with one dream left in it, a plain one. {He} says it is to be given to the next sleeper who cannot sleep.

choices.text: Accept the satchel

effects.log: You become a courier of dreams for a night, then a month. The satchel never empties.

choices.text: Return it with thanks

effects.log: {npc} nods. The dream-paths are better with one more friend in them.

events.text: The stale dreams from the cart are dreams of the dead. {npc} says they are not nightmares in costume after all; they are the dreams of those who died with something unsaid. {He} asks if you will deliver them.

choices.text: Deliver one to a living child of the dead

effects.log: The child wakes laughing and tells their mother. A blessing, however late.

choices.text: Decline, and say a quiet prayer

effects.log: You say it. The dreams stir in the cart, peaceful at last.

events.text: A chunk of amber the size of a loaf sits on a shelf of a dream-collector in the Silent Hall. Inside it, preserved like a fly, is a dream: a field at dusk, a small figure waving. The collector says it is not for sale, but you may look.

choices.text: Look closely

effects.log: The figure turns its head. It waves at you. You wave back before you can stop yourself.

choices.text: Ask whose dream it is

effects.log: The collector hesitates. It was taken from a dying god, they say, as a kindness. Nobody has dared to wake it.

choices.text: Thank them and go

effects.log: The amber glows as you leave, as if sighing.

events.text: The collector offers to let you wake the dream, for an hour. You must hold the amber to your forehead and not speak. You will be inside it, a visitor, a ghost in someone else's peace.

choices.text: Take the hour

effects.log: You walk through the dusk field. The small figure takes your hand. You walk together until the grass turns violet and the hour is up.

choices.text: Decline the hour

effects.log: Some dreams are too tender to walk in. The collector nods, a little relieved.

events.text: The dying god, the collector admits, is still alive: asleep in the Hall, in a quiet ward, and the amber is a copy of what they are dreaming. If someone were to wake the dreamer, the dream would end.

choices.text: Visit the dreamer and sit by the bed

effects.log: You sit. The dreamer sleeps on, a small smile on their face. You do not wake them.

choices.text: Leave the matter to the healers

effects.log: The healers keep their own counsel. You are not sure it is the right call, and you do not intervene.

events.text: Years later the amber glows hot one night and the collector sends for you. The dreamer has died in their sleep, smiling, and the dream is yours to carry out of the Hall, as the last request. They left only one instruction: do not break it.

choices.text: Carry the amber to a field at dusk

effects.log: You carry it to a field at the right hour. The amber warms, and then softens, and a small figure steps out and waves, and is gone. The field smells of rain.

choices.text: Keep it on your shrine shelf, unbroken

effects.log: It sits there for ages, glowing. People bring their own dreams to lay beside it.

events.text: The collector sends you a note, years on: the amber is gone, taken in the night. They suspect a god who wanted a dream of their own. You should know that the dream, when stolen, woke up and sang a very small song.

choices.text: Go looking for the thief

effects.log: You find them in a distant shrine, weeping over the amber. They return it, ashamed, and the dream sings on.

choices.text: Let them keep it, for now

effects.log: A dream does what it must. You trust the amber to find its own way home.

events.text: A nightmare has wandered out of Mongsa's paths and into your waking domain. It looks like a heap of wet black wool with a face, and it is very sad. Villagers below have been waking with the cry on their lips.

choices.text: Approach it slowly

effects.log: The nightmare shrinks from you. It is cold to the touch and trembling.

choices.text: Set a snare of moonlit thread

effects.log: You lay a snare of silver thread across the nightmare's path. It will hold, but not for long.

choices.text: Warn your worshippers to sleep with a lamp lit

effects.log: The lamp, warm and small, keeps the worst away. The nightmare moves on slowly.

events.text: The nightmare tells you, in a voice made of rain on a window, that it was left behind. Its dreamer died, and it has nowhere to go. It does not want to frighten anyone; it wants only to be used.

choices.text: Calm it with a lullaby of your own

ok.log: The nightmare softens. It curls at your feet and becomes something almost like a cat.

fail.log: The lullaby cracks on a bad note, and the nightmare screams. The valley wakes in a sweat.

choices.text: Offer to take it home to Mongsa

effects.log: The nightmare agrees, tremulously. You walk it back along the silver path, past gentler dreams.

events.text: The snare holds the nightmare. It pulls, and the thread is a ladder of cold. It looks at you with its long wet face and says: please. You see that the thread hurts it.

choices.text: Loosen the thread

effects.log: It slumps, trembling. You sit beside it and say nothing, until it is calm.

choices.text: Tighten the snare and take it to the Hall

effects.log: The Hall receives it with gravity. The nightmare is put in a ward, and you are thanked, coolly.

events.text: Mongsa wakes for the length of a breath, and the whole path hums. They take the nightmare from you gently, like a lost child, and say thank you in a voice so slow it takes three days to arrive.

choices.text: Wait for the whole thank-you

effects.log: You wait. When it arrives, it is a small dream, yours alone, of a long afternoon and a cat.

choices.text: Bow and withdraw

effects.log: The Sleeper is sleeping again before you reach the bend.

events.text: The nightmare, left to run wild, stays near your domain for a season. Your worshippers sleep badly. At the end, it simply fades, in a corner of a barn, unseen. You attend the fading and hold its cold hand.

choices.text: Sit with it to the end

effects.log: It dissolves like frost. A last whisper: I am sorry I frightened them.

choices.text: Leave it to its rest

effects.log: Rest is rest. You are tired too.

events.text: A worshipper, {npc}, fell asleep on the steps of your shrine a month ago and has not woken. The shrine-keeper has been feeding {him} broth by spoon. The healers say {he} is not ill. {He} is lost in a path of Mongsa.
events.arc: The Pilgrim Who Did Not Wake

choices.text: Enter the dream-path to find {him}

effects.log: You lie down by the steps and let the silver grass take you.

choices.text: Ask Mongsa's priests for a guide

effects.log: A drowsy priest brings a lantern and a ball of silver thread and a firm instruction not to let go.

choices.text: Keep feeding {him} broth

effects.log: It is gentle, ordinary care. You do it until your hands remember.

events.text: In the dream you find {npc} sitting on a stone at the edge of a calm lake, content. {He} says {he} wants to stay. In the waking world {he} had many sorrows. Here, none. {He} asks you not to be angry.
events.arc: The Pilgrim Who Did Not Wake

choices.text: Sit and listen to the whole of it

effects.log: You listen to all {he} has lost. It is a great deal. When {he} finishes you are both crying.

choices.text: Convince {him} to wake

ok.log: You say what is true, plainly. {npc} nods slowly, and stands.

fail.log: You say it clumsily. {npc} turns back to the lake, offended.

events.text: The lantern leads you to the lake. The silver thread is long, and you hold the end. At the lake sits {npc}, content. The priest's voice, from far away, says: you may call {him} once.
events.arc: The Pilgrim Who Did Not Wake

choices.text: Call {him} by name

effects.log: The name rings across the water. {npc} turns and, slowly, rises.

choices.text: Wait for another hour

effects.log: You wait. The lake is beautiful. {npc} does not look up.

events.text: {npc} wakes on the shrine steps at dawn, thin and clear-eyed. {He} stays at the shrine as a keeper for a season, then goes home. {He} has not been sleeping much, {he} says, but when {he} does, {he} dreams of a lake, and is content with just a visit.
events.arc: The Pilgrim Who Did Not Wake

choices.text: Wish {him} well at the gate

effects.log: {He} waves from the road. A small, easy wave.

choices.text: Give {him} a lamp to keep by the bed

effects.log: {He} takes the lamp, and keeps it lit for forty years.

events.text: {npc} stays. In the world above, the body goes quiet and then gone. In the dream, {he} sits by the lake, content. You visit once a year, in sleep, and sit with {him} for an hour. It is not a bad end, and not a good one, and you learn to carry both.
events.arc: The Pilgrim Who Did Not Wake

choices.text: Keep visiting, in sleep, for as long as you are able

effects.log: You do. The lake, in time, is part of your own dreams.

choices.text: Say goodbye and do not return

effects.log: You say it at the water's edge. {He} nods. It is a kind goodbye.

events.text: A tide-ox calf has lost its herd and stands at the edge of a drop-off, lowing in a voice like a bell underwater. Its mother is somewhere in the dark, calling back, too far for either to hear.

choices.text: Carry the calf to its mother

effects.log: It is heavy, solemn, and warm. The herd lows in welcome when you arrive.

choices.text: Call the mother to you

effects.log: Your voice carries. The mother ox comes, grumbling, to collect the wandering calf.

events.text: A chapel of salt stands on the seabed, a hundred years old and still white. A pilgrim crab keeps the door, and for a pinch of faith will let you ring the bell and wish.

choices.text: Pay a pinch and wish

effects.log: The bell rings once. The wish is small and honest, and the crab approves.

choices.text: Ask the crab how the chapel was built

effects.log: It tells you a long story involving a god, a flood and a very large spoon.

events.text: A school of lamp-fish drifts through the deep, each carrying a tiny flame. They gather round you in a ring, curious, and try to read your face by their own light.

choices.text: Hold still and let them read

effects.log: They flicker over you, then settle in a pattern that spells, with some effort, hello.

choices.text: Follow them to the light-field

effects.log: They lead you to a meadow of glowing weed where the sea hums in harmony.

events.text: A wreck on the seabed has become the home of a small god of a single ship, who is delighted to have a guest. They serve you a very soggy tea and show you the logbook of a voyage that ended a thousand years ago.

choices.text: Read the logbook aloud

effects.log: The god sits up straighter. It is the first time the log has been read since the voyage.

choices.text: Drink the tea out of politeness

effects.log: It is horrid. The god beams. You have made a friend for life.

events.text: The kelp forest on the sea-floor has grown into a maze, and the maze has a heart: a clearing with a stone chair where a sea-turtle the size of a house sits, pondering. It asks you three riddles about patience.

choices.text: Answer all three

effects.log: The turtle approves, slowly. It gives you a barnacle, which is a kind of blessing.

choices.text: Sit and ponder with it

effects.log: You ponder for an hour. The turtle shifts, pleased. It has found a new thinker.

events.text: Letters drift in the deep currents, sealed in glass: messages thrown from ships that never reached land. A school of small silver fish herds them gently toward the shore, one by one, to be found.

choices.text: Help herd the letters

effects.log: You nudge a dozen shoreward. Somewhere, someone will find one and cry.

choices.text: Read one letter

effects.log: It is a love letter, badly spelled. You tuck it back in its bottle and send it on.

events.text: An anchor the size of a mountain stands upright in the silt, chained to nothing. Around it hang the offerings of passing sailors, and every year the anchor sinks a hair deeper. A tide-priest says it is the sea's own promise to stay.

choices.text: Add a small offering

effects.log: You tie a ribbon on the chain. It glows briefly and fades.

choices.text: Ask what it is anchored to

effects.log: The priest says: nothing, and that is the point. Everyone has to keep trusting it.

events.text: Shells on the sea-floor hum a note when the tide turns, each one a different pitch, and a choirmaster crab conducts them with a claw. Today the third shell is off key.

choices.text: Tune the shell with a pinch of sand

effects.log: The crab bows. The choir rings true, a clear chord rising through the water.

choices.text: Leave the flat shell as it is

effects.log: The choir includes it. The crab shrugs: a choir is a choir.

events.text: A ghost of a pearl diver still dives the shallows, holding breath for impossible lengths. The diver does not know about being dead, and asks if you have seen a basket.

choices.text: Help find the basket

effects.log: You find it caught in a rock. The diver takes it, thanks you and, finally, sets it down.

choices.text: Tell the diver gently what has happened

effects.log: A long quiet. Then the diver smiles, swims up, and does not come back.

events.text: A hot vent on the sea-floor wheezes and clicks. A colony of pale shrimp lives on it, and they worship it. They ask you, politely, whether you are the vent's god.

choices.text: Say no, but you will tell the vent's god they asked

effects.log: The shrimp are satisfied. They name you a messenger.

choices.text: Say yes, for the afternoon

effects.log: They bring you offerings of rock and warm water. It is, somehow, very moving.

events.text: In a dream-path there is a door in the middle of the grass, standing alone. Behind it is a pillow on a bed. A note on the pillow says: you may lie down here for an hour; no one will come.

choices.text: Lie down for the hour

effects.log: It is the best hour of rest you have had in an age. You wake refreshed, as if from a week.

choices.text: Leave it for someone who needs it more

effects.log: You close the door softly. Somewhere a more tired god will find it.

events.text: In Mongsa's paths the cats are very large and walk in a long slow line, tails curled, eyes shut. You fall into step among them. Nobody has ever asked where they go.

choices.text: Walk with them till dawn

effects.log: They end at a sun-warmed wall. They lie down, all at once, and so do you.

choices.text: Ask the nearest cat where they go

effects.log: It opens one eye. Here, it says, and closes it again.

events.text: A stair in the dream-path goes up into a cloud, and at the top you can hear a faint murmur, as of a distant sea. A sleepy attendant says it is the way to the dreams of the Upper Realm; not for gods, they add, only for visitors.

choices.text: Peer over the top

effects.log: A distant, windy brightness, and the smell of rain. You wave and descend.

choices.text: Stay below and listen

effects.log: You listen to the murmur. It is enough.

events.text: In a dream-path you find a house you lived in once, before you were a god. The kitchen is exactly as it was. A kettle is warming. Someone is humming in the next room, and you do not go in.

choices.text: Sit at the table and wait

effects.log: The humming stops. A warm cup appears. You drink in silence, and wake at the last sip.

choices.text: Open the door to the next room

effects.log: The room is empty, and the humming is the kettle. You laugh and cry at once.

events.text: An owl in a dream-library lends you a book you have not read yet, from a shelf marked for tomorrow. It asks that you return it before you wake. You do not finish it, but you remember the first line.

choices.text: Read until the page burns

effects.log: You read the first chapter. It is about you, and it is kind.

choices.text: Return it unopened

effects.log: The owl takes it back with a nod. Some tomorrows are better surprised.

events.text: In Mongsa's paths there is a room where it always rains, softly, indoors. A small god of weariness sits there with a cup. They say they come to listen. You may sit, if you do not talk.

choices.text: Sit quietly in the rain

effects.log: The rain asks nothing. After an hour, you could weep for the sheer ease.

choices.text: Ask what they are listening for

effects.log: The god says: to hear that things end. It is more comforting than you thought.

events.text: A stream in the dream-path runs backward. Where it begins, it is shallow and cold and full of small fish; where it ends, at a rock, it is deep and warm and full of unborn songs.

choices.text: Drink from the end

effects.log: The water is sweet and strange. You wake with a half-finished song in your head.

choices.text: Walk the stream to its source

effects.log: It is a long, quiet walk. At the source is a small stone, and a bird, and nothing else.

events.text: The dream-paths ripple with a deep slow wind that comes from Mongsa's breathing. It carries pollen of dreams, sneezes of tiny wonders, and the faint smell of toast.

choices.text: Walk upwind to find the toast

effects.log: You find nothing but a plate of toast on a rock. It is warm and perfect. You eat it with gratitude.

choices.text: Hold out a hand to catch a dream-pollen

effects.log: A single spark settles on your palm and sinks in, leaving a small warm patch.

events.text: In a dream-path, children made of fog play a game with no rules, running in circles and shrieking with joy. When they see you, they shout: you are it! You are, very certainly, it.

choices.text: Chase them, laughing

effects.log: They scatter like a flock. You never catch one, and it does not matter.

choices.text: Hide and let them find you

effects.log: They find you in four breaths. You are delighted. They are insufferable.

events.text: There is a place at the edge of the realm that has no name, because it was there before names. It is not dark, and not light, and not cold. Things you hold up to it forget what they were called, for a moment.

choices.text: Step in, and hold your own name tightly

effects.log: You say it over and over. At the centre it goes quiet, and you stand there simply, a thing without a word.

choices.text: Throw a pebble in and watch

effects.log: The pebble goes in, and does not come out. A moment later a small round stone, nameless, rolls out another side.

choices.text: Walk the rim and look

effects.log: You walk it for a day. Everything you pass on the rim looks slightly newer than it should.

events.text: At the centre you hear a sound like a held breath about to be let go. Something here is waiting to be named, and has waited since before the first god.

choices.text: Offer it a name

effects.log: You give it a plain one: Hello. It stirs. The air tastes of rain on stone.

choices.text: Refuse, and ask what it wants

effects.log: It has no words. It leans, a little, toward you, like a plant to light.

events.text: The small stone sits in your pocket and will not be named. Every name you try slides off. It is warm, and heavy, and quietly pleased. You realise it is the first stone, or the last.

choices.text: Set it on your shrine, unnamed

effects.log: It sits there. Visitors feel something and cannot say what. They leave offerings anyway.

choices.text: Return it to the place

effects.log: You carry it back and set it at the rim. It rolls in of its own accord.

events.text: The Place, named Hello, begins to change. Soft shapes rise at the edges: a bank, a tree, a pool. A young domain is forming, a small one, a gentle one, and it has your voice in it. The courts will want to know.

choices.text: Keep the new domain a secret

effects.log: It grows in the dark, a hidden meadow in the realm's corner. You visit it sometimes. It is yours.

choices.text: Report it to the high court

effects.log: The court is thrown into chaos, then delight. A new domain! The name Hello is gravely recorded.

events.text: You ask the Place what it wants and it never says, but over the years it leans a little closer to you each visit. At last, you understand: it wants to be seen, not named. You sit with it and watch, and say nothing.

choices.text: Keep visiting, and keep watching

effects.log: It becomes a quiet practice. Your qi deepens, your worries thin. The Place, you suspect, is grateful.

choices.text: Mark the Place on the wardens' map

effects.log: You mark it simply: here. The wardens, perplexed, leave it as is.

events.text: Hwarin's ember-cranes migrate once a century from the First Hearth to a cold lake in the north. Their feathers glow like coals, and they leave small fires in their wake. This year they are late, and the lake is freezing.

choices.text: Go to the lake and light a beacon

effects.log: You build a beacon of dry pine on the shore. It crackles, bright, and you wait.

choices.text: Fly south to find the flock

effects.log: You find them circling a burnt tower, undecided. Their leader has a cracked beak.

choices.text: Wait at the Hearth for news

effects.log: A messenger sparrow arrives at last: the cranes are lost in smoke.

events.text: The cranes see the beacon through the haze and descend, a long red V of living coals. They land on the ice and the ice hisses, steams, and begins to give way. They are exhausted, and the lake is a lifeline.

choices.text: Feed them embers from your shrine

effects.log: They eat greedily. Their feathers brighten. The leader dips its head to you.

choices.text: Keep the beacon burning all night

effects.log: You keep it burning, and by dawn the lake is steaming gently. The cranes sleep in a ring around you.

events.text: The leader's beak is cracked from tip to base, and each wingbeat sends sparks into the wind. The crane cannot lead them farther. The others look to you, in the way of birds.

choices.text: Mend the beak with warm resin and a prayer

ok.log: The crack closes. The leader flexes its beak and lets out a call like a struck bell.

fail.log: The resin spills. The beak stays broken, but the leader nods, forgiving.

choices.text: Offer to lead them yourself

effects.log: You fly ahead through the smoke, a god-shaped beacon. The cranes follow.

events.text: At last the flock reaches the lake and the ice breaks in a ring of steam, and the cranes dance on the shore, a stamping red ballet. Hwarin's voice reaches you on the wind: well done. You can feel that warmth like a hand on the shoulder.

choices.text: Dance with them, badly

effects.log: You stamp and flap. The cranes are polite about it. Hwarin laughs from three domains away.

choices.text: Watch from the shore and take a feather

effects.log: The leader drops a single glowing feather at your feet. It will not burn you, and it never goes cold.

events.text: The cranes winter on the lake. In spring they leave in a gold line, trailing smoke like a banner. The lake keeps a warm patch on its surface, and the local fish are very pleased with themselves.

choices.text: Raise a small shrine on the shore

effects.log: Fishermen bring offerings. The shrine's lamp is never cold.

choices.text: Wave them off and walk home

effects.log: The sky is empty, then not. It is a good way to end a journey.

events.text: On the highest ridge of the Sky domain a herd of star-stags grazes, antlers branching into constellations. Cheonho counts them each night while hanging the stars. Tonight there is one fewer, and the herd keeps looking at the same patch of dark.

choices.text: Count them yourself

effects.log: You count three times. Thirty-six. One missing. A young hind, by the pattern of the antlers.

choices.text: Ask the herd where the hind went

effects.log: The old stag lowers its antlers, and the stars on them dim. Something has called the hind away.

choices.text: Watch the dark patch

effects.log: The dark patch is a gap in the sky, small and round and faintly warm.

events.text: You find the hind on a cold ledge of the sky, antlers tangled in the cord of a fallen star. The hind is frightened, and the star burns slowly, pulling toward the horizon. There is not long.

choices.text: Cut the cord with a clean strike

ok.log: The cord parts. The hind leaps clear, and the star drifts on, bright and harmless.

fail.log: The cord whips. A cut across your arm, and the hind bolts, shaking free.

choices.text: Calm the hind until the star burns out

effects.log: You sing softly. The star dims, tired, and the cord slackens by itself.

events.text: The old stag shows you a trail of tiny hoofprints in the starlight leading to a cold ledge. It will not go itself. A stag of the Sky does not leave the ridge. You must go, and be careful.

choices.text: Follow the prints

effects.log: They end at the fallen star. A frightened hind lies tangled in its cord.

choices.text: Ask Cheonho to send a hand

effects.log: Cheonho sends a patient attendant. Together you rescue the hind, but you do not feel quite so brave.

events.text: The hind returns to the herd with a new gleam on the antlers: a little constellation that was not there before, shaped, you think, very like a hand. Cheonho names it for you, with a gruff smile.

choices.text: Accept the naming with thanks

effects.log: It hangs in the sky for a thousand years: the Helping Hand. You see it on clear nights.

choices.text: Ask that it be named for the hind instead

effects.log: Cheonho blinks, then nods. The Hind, it is called, and it is worn proudly.

events.text: The hurt arm heals slowly, and the hind, healed, returns to find you and presents you with a shed antler. It is as long as your forearm and hums faintly with the stars in it.

choices.text: Hang the antler in your shrine

effects.log: It sings quietly at night. Visitors say it sounds like distant water.

choices.text: Carry it as a staff

effects.log: The antler fits your hand. It is as light as a thought and as sure as a signpost.

events.text: An old boar crosses your domain every autumn along the same path, through the same gap in the same wall. When it sees you it stops, and bows, a little oddly, as if to someone else. Someone who stood where you stand.
events.arc: The Beast That Remembers the God Before You

choices.text: Bow back

effects.log: The boar snorts, surprised, and goes on. You feel as if you have passed an exam.

choices.text: Follow it along the path

effects.log: It leads you to a mossy stone you have never noticed in your own domain. A name is cut in it, worn almost away.

choices.text: Let it pass without comment

effects.log: The boar passes, bowing to a ghost. You are strangely moved.

events.text: The name on the stone is the name of the god who held your domain before you. You have been told they simply faded. The boar says otherwise, in a rumble of old grammar: they went to ask a question, and did not come back.
events.arc: The Beast That Remembers the God Before You

choices.text: Ask where they went to ask it

effects.log: The boar paws the ground, northwards, toward a place the court calls nothing. You have never been told of it.

choices.text: Say you will carry on their work

effects.log: The boar lowers its head. It has been waiting for someone to say this for an age.

events.text: You and the boar fall into a ritual: it crosses, you bow, it snorts. Over seasons the boar grows friendlier. One autumn it stays, and eats from your hand, and you realise it has chosen you.
events.arc: The Beast That Remembers the God Before You

choices.text: Accept the boar as a companion

effects.log: The boar follows you home and becomes a fixture of your shrine. It is rude to visitors and loved by children.

choices.text: Let the boar come and go as it likes

effects.log: It comes and goes. You like it that way.

events.text: You walk north, and at the end of the road is a plain well. The previous god's question is carved on the lip: what do the faithful want? It has a hundred answers scratched around it, and none are crossed out.
events.arc: The Beast That Remembers the God Before You

choices.text: Scratch your own answer

effects.log: You scratch: to be heard. The well hums. The boar, behind you, snorts approval.

choices.text: Leave the question unanswered

effects.log: You leave it open. Some questions are better asked than answered, and this one is still being asked.

events.text: You do the work the old god left unfinished, a long plain job of repairing walls and clearing wells and keeping the paths. It is not glorious. The boar follows you through every task, grunting.
events.arc: The Beast That Remembers the God Before You

choices.text: Dedicate the work to the old god

effects.log: You carve their name on a new stone beside the old, and a line: carried on.

choices.text: Do it quietly, without a stone

effects.log: The work is its own monument. The boar bows to it.

events.text: On a mud-bank in a marsh of your domain stands a shrine built by herons: a ring of reeds, a single stone, a feather on top. {npc}, a naturalist god who studies them, sits nearby with a notebook and a thermos. The herons are worshipping something. {He} does not know what.

choices.text: Sit beside {him} and watch

effects.log: You sit. The herons bow to the stone at dawn, in perfect silence. Whatever they pray to has no name.

choices.text: Ask {him} for the notebook

effects.log: The notebook is full of tidy sketches of herons bowing, with a column of question marks.

choices.text: Leave them to their devotions

effects.log: You nod to the herons. One nods back.

events.text: {npc} slips on the mud, and you catch {him}. The herons, startled, rise in a white cloud and settle again in a circle round you. They bow. They are not bowing to the stone. They are bowing to you.

choices.text: Bow back

effects.log: Fifty herons bow in unison. {npc} drops the thermos in awe.

choices.text: Step out of the circle quickly

effects.log: The herons look confused, then settle. {npc} laughs, helplessly, and writes it all down.

events.text: The question marks in the notebook all lead to one entry: a feather of a heron that died in the marsh three seasons ago. The shrine is for that one. It is a funeral, kept for a year, by birds that cannot count.

choices.text: Lay a reed at the stone

effects.log: The herons watch you do it. One flaps up and lays another beside it.

choices.text: Tell {npc} what you think

effects.log: {He} looks at the notebook for a long time. Then {he} puts it away, and just watches.

events.text: Autumn comes, and the herons leave. The shrine is bare, the stone is cold. {npc} and you stand there. {He} says, softly, that the herons are not worshipping a god; they are worshipping a habit. And that this, {he} supposes, is what a god is.

choices.text: Leave a feather of your own on the stone

effects.log: You set a feather, any feather. When spring comes, there are two feathers on the stone.

choices.text: Ask {him} to put the notebook in the shrine

effects.log: {He} does, wrapped in oilcloth. The shrine now has a library of one.

events.text: {npc} writes up the herons for the court. The court is unmoved. {He} sends you the draft anyway, and a pressed reed from the shrine, and a note that says only: thank you for sitting.

choices.text: Frame the reed in your shrine

effects.log: It hangs where you can see it. It is the least expected kind of faith.

choices.text: Write back, and ask for more sketches

effects.log: {He} sends fourteen. They line your shrine wall for ages.

events.text: At the edge of the Mountain domain, in a cleft that was a fault in the world before the world was cut, lies an egg. It is the size of a hut, grey, warm, humming. Nothing alive has ever hatched from it. Nothing has dared to touch it.

choices.text: Lay a hand on it

effects.log: It is warm as a sleeper. Inside, something stirs, slow and vast.

choices.text: Ask Daeak of the Unmoving Peak about it

effects.log: Daeak says nothing for three days. Then: do not wake it. Nothing more is said.

choices.text: Leave it, and mark the cleft

effects.log: You mark it with a cairn of small stones. The egg hums quietly.

events.text: The egg cracks, a finger-width, and a wind of pure primal air breathes out: older than gods, older than names. It smells of wet stone and the end of the world. The crack widens a hair.

choices.text: Hold the shell closed with your hands

ok.log: You press, and the shell settles. The humming steadies, and the crack hairlines.

fail.log: The shell heaves. You are thrown back and the crack opens a hand's breadth.

choices.text: Sing it a slow lullaby

effects.log: The humming softens. The shell, you think, is listening. The crack hairlines.

events.text: Daeak comes in the night, a vast presence, and sits by the egg without a word. Then Daeak says it is the last of something the first gods agreed to forget. The request is for your help in keeping it so.

choices.text: Agree to take a watch

effects.log: You and Daeak keep the watch in shifts. Years pass. The egg hums on.

choices.text: Tell Daeak you are not the right god for this

effects.log: A nod, not unkindly. Someone else will be found.

events.text: You keep the egg warm and still. It does not hatch. But it grows quieter every year, as if reassured. A hundred years on, you realise it has been dreaming, and its dreams are mild.

choices.text: Place a small shrine beside it

effects.log: Mountain-goats and gods alike now come to sit by the egg. It is a place of strange peace.

choices.text: Seal the cleft with a ring of stones

effects.log: The ring holds. The egg dreams on, undisturbed, and so do you.

events.text: The egg opens a hand's breadth, and something looks out. It is not an animal, or a god, or a monster. It is a small, curious, ancient eye. It blinks at you, and closes again. It does not mean harm.

choices.text: Wait with it until it sleeps again

effects.log: You wait. The eye stays shut. The crack seals itself like a scar.

choices.text: Run, and tell the court

effects.log: The court sends wardens. The egg is gone by the time they arrive, rolled away in the night into some deeper fault.

events.text: There is a valley in the realm where no sound has ever been made. Not a hush: a silence, a presence, older than speech. Birds do not fly over it. Rivers go round. A shrine-keeper at its edge hands you a plug of wool and a bell.

choices.text: Stuff the wool in your ears and enter

effects.log: The world drops away. Your heartbeat is the loudest thing in the realm.

choices.text: Enter without wool, bell in hand

effects.log: The silence closes over you like water. The bell makes no sound when you ring it.

choices.text: Sit at the edge and listen

effects.log: You listen to the silence from the outside. It listens back.

events.text: In the heart of the valley is a single standing stone, and nothing else. When you lay a hand on it, a sound begins, very faint: a first note, tentative. It is a god's first word, never said.

choices.text: Say the word for it

effects.log: You say it aloud, softly. The silence shivers, the stone hums, and a bird, far away, begins to sing.

choices.text: Let it finish the word itself

effects.log: You wait. The note rises over minutes. When it ends, the silence sighs, and returns.

events.text: Without the wool, you hear what the valley is made of: not an absence but a held breath, of every word the first gods did not say. It presses on your ears, patient and enormous. It asks for nothing.

choices.text: Add a word of your own to the held breath

effects.log: You whisper it. It is accepted. The valley, you feel, is a little less full.

choices.text: Withdraw before it is too much

effects.log: You walk out, shaking. The silence follows to the rim, and stops.

events.text: The word you said is heard across the realm. Nobody knows where from. People say it quietly at their meals, and children say it in their sleep. The shrine-keeper at the rim bows to you when you pass.

choices.text: Ask the keeper what the word means

effects.log: The keeper says it has no meaning. It is only the first thing someone said, and everything since has been an answer.

choices.text: Say nothing and accept the thanks

effects.log: The thanks warm like a shawl. The silence in the valley is a little lighter.

events.text: You return to the valley once a decade, and sit by the stone, and listen. Sometimes the note is different. Sometimes it is a bird. Sometimes, once, it was your name, said slowly, in a voice that did not use language.

choices.text: Answer the voice in the same way

effects.log: You answer in no words. The silence deepens, and you feel known.

choices.text: Keep the experience private

effects.log: Some silences are best kept in silence.

events.text: Noegong's nine drums of thunder have a keeper no one speaks of: a toad the size of a cart, who sits under the ninth drum and sounds it with its throat. This year the ninth drum has gone flat, and the toad is sulking.
events.arc: The Drum-Toad of the Nine Drums

choices.text: Ask the toad what is wrong

effects.log: It croaks in a deep, miserable voice. It has caught a cold.

choices.text: Check the drum for damage

effects.log: The drum-skin is sound. The fault is in the toad.

choices.text: Report it to Noegong

effects.log: Noegong sends a messenger with a pot of ginger tea and a kind word.

events.text: The toad sneezes and the whole mountain shakes. A storm, three valleys away, breaks out of season. The ninth drum is the one that closes the thunder; without it, the storm will not stop.
events.arc: The Drum-Toad of the Nine Drums

choices.text: Brew the toad a hot remedy

ok.log: The toad drinks it and rumbles, relieved. The ninth drum rings true, and the storm eases.

fail.log: The brew is too strong. The toad hiccups, and the storm worsens for a night.

choices.text: Sing to the toad until it sleeps

effects.log: You sing for hours. At last it drops off, and with it the storm.

events.text: A burr, wedged under the toad's tongue, is the fault. You find it with a lantern and a long pair of tongs, and pull it out. The toad stares at you with great moist eyes, then lets go a croak so low you feel it in your teeth.
events.arc: The Drum-Toad of the Nine Drums

choices.text: Accept the croak as thanks

effects.log: The drum sounds true. The valley hums with gratitude.

choices.text: Wipe your tongs and leave quietly

effects.log: You leave with a burr in your pocket. A good souvenir.

events.text: Noegong invites you to the drum-feast. A hundred gods stamp and thump the ground, and the toad is given a place of honour at the head. The toad, bashful, keeps its eyes down and nudges a plate of flies toward you.
events.arc: The Drum-Toad of the Nine Drums

choices.text: Eat a fly, for politeness

effects.log: It is crunchy and strange. The toad is delighted, and tells everyone.

choices.text: Toast the toad with a cup of rain

effects.log: The hall roars. The toad croaks, and the whole feast shakes with joy.

events.text: The storm blows itself out in the end, and a stray bolt takes the roof off a granary. The toad recovers, but it holds a grudge against you for a year, and croaks whenever you pass. It is a small price.
events.arc: The Drum-Toad of the Nine Drums

choices.text: Repair the granary roof

effects.log: You spend a week at it. The valley is pleased.

choices.text: Leave a dish of flies for the toad

effects.log: The toad accepts. The grudge ends in a croak of forgiveness.

events.text: A pool in the realm's oldest corner is so still that it shows not your face but your earliest idea of yourself: a small, plain shape with no title. The pool has been there since before titles.

choices.text: Study the shape for an hour

effects.log: You see yourself before you were a god. It is smaller and kinder than you remembered.

choices.text: Drop a pebble in

effects.log: The shape wobbles, and then sits still again. The pool has its dignity.

events.text: The roots of a tree older than the Harvest domain run under the realm in every direction, and wherever one surfaces there is a small shrine nobody built. A root surfaces under your foot and offers, very gently, to trip you.

choices.text: Thank the root and step over it

effects.log: The root withdraws. You have an odd sense of having been approved.

choices.text: Sit on the root and listen

effects.log: It hums. Something enormous and slow is thinking, deep below.

events.text: There is a wind in the realm that blows only in one direction, upward, and has done so since the world was cut. It carries nothing but a faint smell of the time before. Old gods stand in it with their eyes shut.

choices.text: Stand in it with them

effects.log: You stand. Your thoughts lighten, your name loosens. When you open your eyes an hour has passed.

choices.text: Light a lamp in its path

effects.log: The flame leans all the way over and does not go out. A good omen.

events.text: Across a flat of black glass, in the realm's deepest corner, runs a line of footprints bigger than a house. They go in a straight line from nowhere to nowhere. A local god says nobody has seen what made them. Nobody wants to.

choices.text: Pace one out

effects.log: It takes forty steps. At the end you find a petrified flower, delicate as a breath.

choices.text: Follow the line to its end

effects.log: It ends at the edge of the world. A neat, round hole. Nothing comes out.

events.text: In a valley before the domains were cut a bell hangs in the air with no tower, no rope. It rings once a year, on a day nobody has recorded. Today a small crowd of gods has gathered to hear it, with sandwiches.

choices.text: Join the crowd and wait

effects.log: The bell rings. Everyone is quiet. Then everyone resumes sandwiches. It is a good ceremony.

choices.text: Ask what the bell is for

effects.log: An old god shrugs: nothing. That is why we come.

events.text: The salt flats of the old sea stretch away white and silent, and in the distance a figure stands, tall as a tree, facing away. It never moves. When you come close it turns out to be a column of salt in the shape of a god.

choices.text: Leave an offering at its feet

effects.log: A pinch of salt returned to salt. The column seems to lean towards you, politely.

choices.text: Walk around it, once

effects.log: Its face is worn smooth. You feel you have been introduced.

events.text: A cavern in the primal places hums on a single low note. Gods sit inside it to think. A sign at the mouth: please do not hum along; we are trying to find the note. Beneath it, in pencil: it is B.

choices.text: Sit and think in the hum

effects.log: Your thoughts line up, one by one, like ducklings. You find a solution to a problem you had forgotten.

choices.text: Hum along, very softly

effects.log: The cavern grows silent. A stern echo says: shh.

events.text: A small rain cloud, lost from the Sky domain, has drifted into the primal places and cannot find the way home. It follows you in a mournful drizzle. It would, you gather, like to be asked in.

choices.text: Bring it home to the Sky court

effects.log: The cloud trails behind you. At the court gates it brightens, and the guards laugh.

choices.text: Let it rain on your garden

effects.log: The garden loves it. The cloud stays a season and leaves a rainbow.

events.text: Three stones in a ring, black with age, mark a hearth from before there was a First Hearth. No ash, no wood. You put out your hand and feel warmth, as of a fire that was lit a long time ago and has not yet gone out.

choices.text: Warm your hands at the old hearth

effects.log: The warmth travels up your arms. You feel at home in a way you cannot explain.

choices.text: Light a spill from it

effects.log: The spill catches. You carry the flame home. It never needs fuel.

events.text: On a green hill stands a ring of tall stones, each carved with a name that is not a name any more. A young god sits on one, kicking heels. The name is Oh, they say, because that is what people say when they see them.

choices.text: Sit with the young god and talk

effects.log: You hear of the hill, the stones, a thousand things. The young god is lonely and eager.

choices.text: Ask for your name on a stone

effects.log: It is done, wobbly. It is the worst carving in the realm, and you love it.

events.text: A fox of living ember has taken up residence in your hearth. It does not burn the house; it only sits and watches the fire, and occasionally moves a log with its paw, as if correcting your work.

choices.text: Let the fox tend the fire

effects.log: The fire burns better than it has in years. The fox accepts a saucer of oil as thanks.

choices.text: Ask the fox its name

effects.log: It does not answer, but your shrine-keeper later insists it said: Cinder.

events.text: A cloud-ox wanders the Sky domain, grazing on mist and leaving a trail of drizzle. The local herders say that to feed one a handful of salt brings a good spring. This one has a limp.

choices.text: Tend its hoof

effects.log: A thorn. You pull it out. The ox lows deeply and rains a single warm shower on you.

choices.text: Feed it a handful of salt

effects.log: It licks your palm with a rough tongue. Rain follows you home.

events.text: The hound of the Silent Hall sleeps in the vestibule and wakes only when a lie is told within the Hall. Today it has been awake since dawn, ears up, and nobody can find the liar.

choices.text: Sit by the hound and tell only truths

effects.log: The hound watches you for an hour, then lays its head down. A good sign.

choices.text: Scratch its ears

effects.log: It leans into your hand. A court clerk, relieved, confesses a small fib. The hound sleeps.

events.text: Pungnyeon's golden hares come out only at harvest-dusk, a hundred of them, and sit in the wheat in a ring with their ears forward, listening to the grain ripen. If you sit still, you can hear it too.

choices.text: Sit with the hares and listen

effects.log: The grain murmurs as it fills. It is the sound of a thousand small satisfactions.

choices.text: Leave a bowl of milk at the edge

effects.log: The hares come to it after you go. The harvest is generous that year.

events.text: On the Unmoving Peak a goat stands on a ledge no wider than its hooves, facing the abyss. It has stood there longer than the peak has had a name. Daeak calls it the senior pupil.

choices.text: Stand beside it a while

effects.log: You stand. The goat does not look at you. After an hour you understand, a very little, about stillness.

choices.text: Offer it a leaf of mountain-mint

effects.log: It takes the leaf without moving its head, which is impressive.

events.text: A litter of wolf pups of the Wild lie in a bundle in a hollow log; their mother is hunting. Horang's rule is that no god touches a pup. They squeak, in unison, a very small and unfair squeak.

choices.text: Stand guard until the mother wolf returns

effects.log: The mother arrives at dusk, sees you, and gives a single approving nod. The pups nose out to meet the mother.

choices.text: Leave a rabbit by the log

effects.log: The mother finds it. You are not thanked, but you are not bitten.

events.text: A pale cat rides the ferry of the dead every crossing, seated in the prow, eyes closed. Baekun says it does no work. It is, Baekun says, the only passenger who has never been afraid.

choices.text: Sit beside the cat on the next crossing

effects.log: The cat leans against you. For a moment you forget what ferry you are on.

choices.text: Ask Baekun how it got the job

effects.log: A long think. It came with the boat, Baekun says. Boats come with all sorts of things.

events.text: Swans of the Thunder domain nest on the clouds above Noegong's drums, and hatch their eggs in the shock of the strokes. The cygnets come out with a faint crackle in their feathers. They follow you, hopefully.

choices.text: Lead them to a pond

effects.log: They paddle behind you in a crackling line. At the pond they spark with joy.

choices.text: Gently shoo them back

effects.log: They scatter, disappointed, and then forget. Swans are like that.

events.text: A snail of Saengmo's garden carries on its shell a tiny orchard, with apple trees the size of thumbnails. It moves one leaf-length a day. It is almost certainly older than you.

choices.text: Watch it cross the path

effects.log: It takes the whole afternoon. You are a better god for the patience.

choices.text: Hold a leaf out for it

effects.log: It climbs on, trailing its orchard. You carry it across the garden.

events.text: A war-horse of Mujin's stables, retired, grazes in a meadow at the edge of the Thousand Banners. It remembers every battle and none of the reasons. It leans on the fence beside you and sighs.

choices.text: Scratch its neck and say nothing

effects.log: The horse leans in. A veteran, too tired to speak, grateful for company.

choices.text: Ask it about the old campaigns

effects.log: It snorts a long, windy snort that somehow carries a battle-cry, a joke and a lullaby.

events.text: A moth the size of a plate lands on your shoulder at the edge of sleep. It is a moth of Mongsa's paths, and it has come, it seems, to look at your dreams. It reads them like a menu.

choices.text: Let it feed

effects.log: It takes a nibble of a minor worry. You wake lighter.

choices.text: Offer it a dream of its choosing

effects.log: It selects a plain one: a warm kitchen. You never see that dream again.

events.text: The gulls of the Tide Keeper's coast carry messages in their beaks, small rolled slips in a code only the tide-priests know. A gull drops one at your feet by mistake. It is marked urgent and smells of fish.

choices.text: Return it to the gull and point at the priests

effects.log: The gull glares and flaps away. The slip arrives, late, and the priests are cross.

choices.text: Read it

effects.log: It says: please send more fish. You laugh, and send more fish.

events.text: Once a year the Green Assembly holds its sacred hunt, and no beast is ever taken. The hunters track a single animal through the wood at dawn, and the one who finds it first lays a hand on its flank and gives it a blessing. This year the quarry is a white fox, and it has not been seen in a week.

choices.text: Track the fox by its prints

effects.log: The prints run in a circle round a hollow oak. The fox is playing with you.

choices.text: Leave an offering and wait

effects.log: You set out a dish of milk and sit. The wood is very quiet.

choices.text: Join the other hunters at the horns

effects.log: You ride out with the field, laughing, in a long green line.

events.text: The fox leads you into a clearing where a fallen hunter lies against a root, gasping: a young god who strayed from the line. The fox sits beside them, ears flat. The blessing, this year, may be for someone else.

choices.text: Tend the fallen hunter first

effects.log: You bind a sprained ankle with moss and bark. The hunter weeps with relief, and the fox watches you.

choices.text: Lay the blessing on the hunter, not the fox

effects.log: The hunter is blessed with strong bones. The fox flicks its tail and trots off, content.

events.text: Waiting pays: the fox comes to you, sits on your foot and falls asleep. It is warm as a loaf. The horns sound in the distance. You are, undeniably, first.

choices.text: Lay your hand on its flank and give the blessing

effects.log: You bless it with a long winter and a warm den. The fox yawns and wakes with a tiny, smug expression.

choices.text: Let it sleep, and tell no one

effects.log: You sit with the fox till dusk. The horns die. The hunt ends without a winner, and without a loser.

events.text: The Assembly's feast that night is loud and green. The winner is announced with a flourish, and it is you, or not you, depending on who you ask. Saengmo, Mother of Seeds, presents you with a seed in a clay pot. It is a seed of kindness, and it will grow only if watered.

choices.text: Plant it in your shrine garden

effects.log: In spring a small pale flower opens. It smells of the first morning of the year.

choices.text: Give the seed to the hunter you helped

effects.log: The young god plants it by their door. It grows into a hedge that keeps off bad luck.

events.text: Years on, the young god you tended becomes a hunt-master and invites you to ride at their right hand. The fox, now old and grey, walks ahead of the line. It stops at your horse and looks up, and sneezes.

choices.text: Accept the place of honour

effects.log: You ride beside the master through the wood. The fox leads. It is the finest hunt in memory.

choices.text: Ride at the back and enjoy the day

effects.log: You ride at the tail with the cooks and the children. It is the best seat in the field.

events.text: A pale beast has gotten out of a sealed heaven, through a seal the wardens swear was never opened. It is the size of a draught-horse, with a shining coat the colour of old coins. It has been seen at three shrines, eating the bread offerings and leaving small, perfect hoofprints.
events.arc: The Beast From the Copper Meadow

choices.text: Track it along the shrine road

effects.log: The trail is easy: crumbs, hoofprints, a trail of shrine-keepers scratching their heads.

choices.text: Ask the wardens how it got out

effects.log: They say it was never in. They are, you find, lying badly.

choices.text: Leave the beast to the wardens

effects.log: The wardens will mention it in their next report, in a year or two.

events.text: You find the beast in a barn, asleep in the hay, its copper coat steaming. It is frightened, not fierce. It has the look of a creature that has never seen a roof. When you come close, it lifts its head and shows you a long, patient eye.
events.arc: The Beast From the Copper Meadow

choices.text: Slip a halter of silver thread over its head

ok.log: The halter settles. The beast sighs and lets itself be led, docile as a lamb.

fail.log: The beast startles and bolts, knocking you into the hay. It crashes through the barn wall.

choices.text: Sit in the hay with it for an hour

effects.log: You sit. It watches. At last it lays its head across your knees.

events.text: The wardens admit it, red-faced: they opened the seal themselves, a crack, to let the herd out for air. Most of the herd came back. One did not. The wardens ask, humbly, for your help in bringing it home.
events.arc: The Beast From the Copper Meadow

choices.text: Agree, and keep their secret

effects.log: You promise silence. They bow, ashamed and grateful.

choices.text: Tell them to report themselves to the court

effects.log: They flinch, but they will. You have given them a hard kind of kindness.

events.text: You lead the beast back along the shrine road, past a hundred curious faces. At the seal, the wardens open the door and the whole herd stands waiting inside, copper in the dusk. The escaped one trots in, then looks back at you and, to your surprise, trots out again.
events.arc: The Beast From the Copper Meadow

choices.text: Let it stay with you for a season

effects.log: The beast follows you about your shrine like a cat. Children climb on it. It seems, finally, at peace.

choices.text: Walk it back in, and close the door gently

effects.log: It goes in. The seal closes. You hear the herd let out a breath, like a wave.

events.text: The beast has bolted, through the barn wall and into the night. It leaves a trail of broken fences and startled geese. By dawn it has vanished into the high pastures, and you are left to pay the farmer's bill.
events.arc: The Beast From the Copper Meadow

choices.text: Pay for the barn out of your own shrine's store

effects.log: The farmer is satisfied. Word spreads that you are a god who pays debts.

choices.text: Search the high pastures for a week

effects.log: You find the beast at last, grazing contentedly. It follows you home like a lamb.

events.text: Each autumn the Sea domain drives the tide-oxen from the deep pastures to the winter shelf. It is called a hunt, though nobody harms an ox: you sing them up the slope and the oldest cow leads. This year the lead cow is late, and the herd is milling at the cliff edge.

choices.text: Dive for the lead cow

effects.log: You find the cow tangled in a net of old lines. It is calm and slightly embarrassed.

choices.text: Sing the herd into line

effects.log: You sing an old tide-song. The oxen listen, shuffle, and start to form a rough column.

choices.text: Wait for the lead cow to arrive

effects.log: The cow arrives at last, grumbling, and the herd opens like a curtain.

events.text: The net is old, heavy and wound with kelp. You cut it free with a knife of shell, one strand at a time. The lead cow shakes off the strands and lows, and the herd answers with a long deep note that you feel in your teeth.

choices.text: Lead the column up the slope beside the cow

effects.log: You walk beside the cow, a god among oxen. The slope is long and your legs ache.

choices.text: Let the cow lead and follow at the back

effects.log: You trail the herd. The calves nudge you along, in the nicest way.

events.text: The singing works, but it works too well. The oxen sway in time, and sway too far, and the front rank drifts toward the cliff. A calf stumbles. You have to change the song, and quickly.

choices.text: Switch to a firmer marching song

ok.log: The oxen snap to attention, as it were, and the column steadies. The calf is back in line.

fail.log: You lose the tune. The column breaks and a few oxen tumble down the shelf in a tangle.

choices.text: Wade in and push the calf upright

effects.log: The calf, shocked, trots back to its mother. You are wet and winded.

events.text: At the winter shelf the herd settles, and Haeryong, Keeper of Tides, inspects them one by one, as is the custom. The Keeper stops at the lead cow, says nothing, and pats its neck. Then, to your astonishment, Haeryong bows to you.

choices.text: Bow back, deeply

effects.log: Haeryong smiles, a rare thing. The oxen low in chorus. It is a very good autumn.

choices.text: Offer Haeryong a cup of your own shrine's brew

effects.log: A sip, a wince, and a polite finish. A friendship begins.

events.text: You are wet, tired and covered in kelp. At the shelf the tide-priests give you a blanket and a bowl of fish stew. The lead cow lies beside you, sighing. You fall asleep against the warm flank, and sleep the sleep of the useful.

choices.text: Wake at dawn and help herd the stragglers

effects.log: There are three. You find them behind a rock, playing. You bring them in, laughing.

choices.text: Sleep on

effects.log: Nobody minds. The oxen are warm.

events.text: The Throne of Storms holds a hunt each spring for a rogue thunderhead: a cloud grown too big and too proud, with a mind of its own. Gods ride lightning-colts after it, with nets of wind and ropes of rain. The cloud has already lamed two riders.

choices.text: Take a colt and ride out

effects.log: The colt is warm and fizzing. It bucks, and then settles. The sky is wide.

choices.text: Study the cloud's habits from a ridge

effects.log: It circles. Every third circle it dips toward a certain valley, and then thinks better of it.

choices.text: Watch the hunt from the spectator terraces

effects.log: The riders streak past, small and bright. The cloud grumbles. It is a fine show.

events.text: You ride into the thunderhead's shadow. Wind tears at you, hail drums the saddle, and the cloud turns its great grey face to look at you. It does not want to be caught. It wants, you realise, to go home.

choices.text: Stay in the saddle and hold the net

ok.log: The colt shies but you hold. The net settles, light as breath, and the cloud stops.

fail.log: A bolt takes the colt's shoe off and throws you into the rain. You tumble a long way.

choices.text: Turn back and speak to the cloud

effects.log: You pull up and speak. The cloud pauses. It listens, as clouds do, with a slow hum.

events.text: The cloud's circle always dips toward a valley in the Mountain domain. You ride there and find an old dry lake, long parched. The cloud has been trying to rain on it for years, and every time the hunters drive it away.

choices.text: Plead with the Throne to let it rain

effects.log: The Throne considers. After a long silence, a thundering grudging yes.

choices.text: Lead the cloud to the lake yourself

effects.log: You ride beside it. At the dry lake the cloud lets go, a long, grateful rain.

events.text: The cloud rains itself out over the old lake, and the lake fills, and a spring of frogs begins. The hunt ends without a capture, and the Throne of Storms names this the best hunt in a hundred years. You are given a ribbon of lightning.

choices.text: Wear the ribbon at the next court

effects.log: It sparks, a little. The court is impressed and slightly singed.

choices.text: Tie it to the lake's first reed

effects.log: The reed glows for a decade. Frogs sing under it.

events.text: You wake in a ditch, soaked and aching. The colt grazes nearby, ashamed. A passing farmer helps you up and gives you soup. The hunt has gone on without you, and the cloud, they say, got away. It is not a bad outcome.

choices.text: Thank the farmer and offer a blessing

effects.log: Their field yields double that year. The soup was very good.

choices.text: Rest for a season and return

effects.log: You rest. The bruises fade, the pride a little slower.

events.text: Horang, Lord of the Wild, holds a hunt at midwinter that has no quarry and no rules. All beasts and gods run together in the dark, and whoever stops first is asked to sing. You have been invited, for the first time, with a note in paw-print.
events.arc: The Hunt of the Wild Lord

choices.text: Run with the hunt

effects.log: You run with wolves and stags and an enormous slow bear. You do not stop, and neither do they.

choices.text: Watch from the edge

effects.log: The hunt thunders past, a river of breath and fur and starlight. You feel your heart in your teeth.

choices.text: Send regrets and a gift of venison

effects.log: Horang accepts, with a growl. You are not invited again for ten years.

events.text: You run until your lungs burn and the stars wheel. A stag runs beside you, laughing, and a wolf runs on the other side. You begin to understand that nobody is chasing anything. They are running to be together.
events.arc: The Hunt of the Wild Lord

choices.text: Run on, and laugh back

effects.log: You run until dawn. When you stop, you are in a snowy clearing, alive, and filled with something wide and wordless.

choices.text: Stop first, and sing

effects.log: You stop. They all stop. You must sing. You sing the only song you know, a lullaby your shrine-keeper taught you.

events.text: From the edge you see something the runners cannot: the hunt moves in a great loop, and at the loop's centre sits an old white wolf, not running, just sitting. Everyone passes it at a distance of exactly one pace.
events.arc: The Hunt of the Wild Lord

choices.text: Walk into the loop and sit beside the wolf
